title_en: Trump orders federal contractors to check with White House before responding to Congress
title_zh: 特朗普命令联邦承包商在回应国会之前先与白宫核实
summary: President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统指示联邦承包商就国会的询问向白宫咨询，并隐瞒他的任何信息。
body_en: Trump moves to limit contractors contact with Congress : NPR

Trump moves to limit contractors contact with Congress President Trump is directing federal contractors to consult the White House about inquiries from Congress and to withhold any communications that his administration considers privileged.
President Trump speaks at a news conference in the James Brady Press Briefing Room of the White House, Friday, Nov. 20, 2026, in Washington. Jacquelyn Martin/AP hide caption

NEW YORK (AP) — President Donald Trump is directing federal contractors and subcontractors to consult with his administration about inquiries they receive from Congress and to withhold any communications that the White House considers privileged, according to a new executive order .

The companies must also coordinate with the White House and U.S. agencies on "appropriate responses" to any such requests, the order issued late Friday says. If they fail to comply, the White House warns their contracts could be terminated and their future work with the federal government suspended.

The order is the Republican administration's latest effort to resist what are expected to be wide-ranging and aggressive oversight efforts from Democrats when they take over Congress in January. Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets , noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Trump's family, particularly at the Pentagon.

White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations initiated by Democrats.

Trump's counsel, Will Scharf, told federal agencies on Monday that they must seek approval from his office and the White House's Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia of California, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to "blatant criminality."

Garcia sent letters this week directing members of Trump's family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.

Responding to the new executive order, Garcia said it was part of the administration's "blatant attack on Congress' constitutional right to conduct oversight." He said that despite efforts to impede investigations, "we're just getting started."

In a fact sheet , the White House framed the new requirements as "protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach," arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by "harassing private companies that contract with the federal government."

Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
The latest executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

body_zh: 特朗普采取行动限制承包商与国会的接触：NPR
特朗普采取行动限制承包商与国会的接触特朗普总统正在指示联邦承包商就国会的询问向白宫咨询，并保留其政府认为有特权的任何通信。
特朗普总统于 2026 年 11 月 20 日星期五在华盛顿白宫詹姆斯·布雷迪新闻发布会室举行的新闻发布会上发表讲话。杰奎琳·马丁/美联社隐藏标题栏
纽约（美联社）——根据一项新的行政命令，唐纳德·特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就国会提出的质询与他的政府进行磋商，并扣留任何白宫认为有特权的通信。
周五晚些时候发布的命令称，这些公司还必须与白宫和美国机构协调，对任何此类请求做出“适当回应”。如果他们不遵守规定，白宫警告他们的合同可能会被终止，并且他们未来与联邦政府的合作可能会暂停。
该命令是共和党政府为抵制民主党在一月份接管国会时预计将采取的广泛而积极的监督措施而采取的最新举措。民主党人已将政府合同作为其首要调查目标之一，并指出联邦资金一直流向与特朗普家族有联系的公司，尤其是五角大楼。
白宫官员已经开始采取措施，对各机构和官员如何回应国会要求施加更多控制，预计民主党将发起大量调查。
特朗普的律师威尔·沙夫周一告诉联邦机构，他们必须获得特朗普办公室和白宫立法事务办公室的批准，然后才能同意出席国会会议。沙夫还在最近给众议院监督委员会民主党领袖、加州众议员罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，一些国会调查可能构成“公然犯罪”。
加西亚本周致函特朗普家族成员和高级政府官员保存文件。沙夫试图驳回这些要求，并在给民主党议员的一封信中指出，他们尚未占多数，无法强迫他们遵守。
加西亚在回应新的行政命令时表示，这是政府“公然攻击国会监督权的宪法权利”的一部分。他说，尽管有人努力阻止调查，但“我们才刚刚开始”。
在一份情况说明书中，白宫将新要求描述为“保护行政特权免遭国会越权”，并认为一些国会领导人试图通过“骚扰与联邦政府签订合同的私营公司”来侵犯行政部门的特权。
两党总统长期以来一直利用行政特权来抵制国会调查，但由于双方对其是否适用存在争议，这些主张可能会引发混乱、旷日持久的法律斗争。行政特权允许总统向法院、国会和公众保留信息，以保护白宫审议的机密性，但这种保护远非绝对。
最新的行政命令适用于所有承包商和分包商，涵盖数以万计的企业。

title_en: Voters oust some sheriffs who signed pacts to help Trump's immigration enforcement efforts
title_zh: 选民罢免了一些签署协议以帮助特朗普移民执法工作的警长
summary: Some sheriffs who aided President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown have been ousted from office by voters
summary_zh: 一些协助唐纳德·特朗普总统镇压移民的警长已被选民赶下台
body_en: Some sheriffs who aided President Donald Trump’s immigration crackdown have been ousted from office by voters
By SARAH RANKIN Associated Press , MIKELLA SCHUETTLER Associated Press , and DAVID A. LIEB Associated Press

GRAHAM, N.C. -- As he ran for sheriff in North Carolina against a longtime incumbent who had joined forces with the Trump administration’s immigration crackdown, Shannon Long found his campaign van was an obstacle with some voters.

The trust between law enforcement and Alamance County's growing Latino community was so fractured, Long said, that the vehicle emblazoned with “sheriff” made it a struggle to get some people to speak with him.

“They’ve been living in fear. They feel like they don’t have a voice. They have been suppressed, oppressed; a lot of them are depressed. So they feel that they live in a community where they don’t belong,” Long, a pastor, business owner and former sheriff’s deputy, told The Associated Press two weeks after defeating Republican Sheriff Terry Johnson in a campaign that some activists, voters and local officials say turned partly on questions about immigration enforcement and the treatment of Latino residents.

Johnson is one of a few sheriffs around the country who were ousted by challengers critical of their cooperation with President Donald Trump’s push for mass deportations of people in the country illegally. While only a smattering, the results could spell trouble for other sheriffs who are seen as participants in Trump’s crackdown and possibly hinder agreements that have become a cornerstone of the administration's efforts.

Johnson was among the first sheriffs to allow his deputies to enforce federal immigration laws under what’s known as a 287(g) agreement with U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement. Long, who ran as an independent, promised to curtail cooperation with ICE, which continues to rely on the cooperative pacts to boost arrest numbers despite a one-time infusion of $75 billion from Congress and hiring about 12,000 officers .

The administration has more than 2,700 such pacts with state and local agencies, up from 135 when Trump began his second term. The agreements, predominantly in the South, have deputized over 29,000 local law officers and resulted in more than 6,600 arrests in July, about 15% of all ICE arrests, according to government data obtained by the Deportation Data Project that was analyzed by the advocacy group fwd.us .

The AP reviewed about 250 elections held this month for sheriffs whose offices had 287(g) agreements, identifying races in Indiana, Maryland, North Carolina, Wisconsin and elsewhere in which ICE pacts played a role in a candidate's defeat. Many sheriffs who ran this year were unopposed. But the ICE agreements could become a focus again in two years, when sheriffs from Florida, Texas and other states with large numbers of 287(g) agreements are up for election.

Alamance County is a longtime Republican stronghold of just under 200,000 residents that sits between Greensboro and the Research Triangle metropolitan area that includes Raleigh, Durham and Chapel Hill. It has become more politically competitive as its population has grown increasingly diverse — from 750 residents who identified as Hispanic in the 1990 census to nearly 25,000 in 2020. The sheriff's office currently participates in the 287(g) program, a spokesman confirmed, though last year it ended an agreement to house ICE detainees.

Johnson, who is white, was first elected in 2002 and has been a prominent and polarizing figure. He has insisted he welcomes lawful immigrants and denied persistent allegations — including in a Justice Department lawsuit over a decade ago that ended with a settlement — that his office racially profiled minority residents.

The county acquired the moniker “No Chance Alamance” because of a perceived sense of unjust policing and a lack of political representation among Black and Latino residents, school board member Seneca Rogers said.

Johnson initially said in a phone call that immigration policy could have contributed to his loss. But in a brief interview later, he said it likely didn't and laid blame with his long tenure and a national political environment that was brutal for Republicans , acutely so in North Carolina , where Democratic former Gov. Roy Cooper flipped a U.S. Senate seat, winning by nearly 20 percentage points. He said he always followed the law and protected public safety.

Activists and longtime residents said the Latino community — and to some extent, the Black community — feared engaging with the sheriff's office and described a sense that non-white residents were far likelier to be pulled over or detained after a traffic stop. Some people were afraid to call 911 or even go to work, said community organizer Leslie Arevalo.

Voter Renee Russell said the sheriff’s cooperation with ICE gave a false impression of Alamance as unwelcoming. She was excited to see fresh leadership. Long will be the county’s first Black sheriff, local media reported.

But Republican state Sen. Amy Galey, whose district includes the county, defended Johnson's record. She said he had worked to improve training opportunities and mental health services. Although Galey didn't think immigration played a big role in the race, she wondered if hard-line ICE tactics elsewhere could have contributed to simmering concerns about law enforcement more broadly.

body_zh: 一些协助唐纳德·特朗普总统镇压移民的警长已被选民赶下台
作者：SARAH RANKIN 美联社、MIKELLA SCHUETTLER 美联社和 DAVID A. LIEB 美联社
北卡罗来纳州格雷厄姆——在竞选北卡罗来纳州警长时，香农·朗发现他的竞选车对一些选民来说是一个障碍。
朗说，执法部门与阿拉曼斯县不断壮大的拉丁裔社区之间的信任如此破裂，以至于这辆印有“警长”字样的车辆很难让一些人与他交谈。
“他们一直生活在恐惧之中。他们觉得自己没有发言权。他们受到镇压、压制；很多人都很沮丧。所以他们觉得自己生活在一个不属于自己的社区，”牧师、企业主和前警长副手朗在一场竞选中击败共和党警长特里·约翰逊两周后告诉美联社，一些活动人士、选民和地方官员称，这场竞选在一定程度上引发了有关移民执法和拉丁裔居民待遇的问题。
约翰逊是全国少数几位被挑战者罢免的警长之一，挑战者批评他们与唐纳德·特朗普总统合作，推动大规模非法驱逐国内人口。虽然只是一小部分，但结果可能会给其他被视为特朗普镇压参与者的警长带来麻烦，并可能阻碍已成为政府努力基石的协议。
约翰逊是第一批允许副手根据与美国移民和海关执法局签署的 287(g) 协议执行联邦移民法的警长之一。朗以独立人士身份参选，他承诺减少与 ICE 的合作，尽管国会一次性注入了 750 亿美元并雇用了约 12,000 名警官，但 ICE 仍继续依靠合作协议来增加逮捕人数。
政府与州和地方机构签订了 2,700 多项此类协议，而特朗普开始第二任期时有 135 项。根据倡导团体 fwd.us 分析的驱逐数据项目获得的政府数据，这些协议主要在南方，已授权超过 29,000 名当地执法人员，并导致 7 月份逮捕了 6,600 多人，约占 ICE 逮捕总数的 15%。
美联社审查了本月举行的约 250 场警长选举，这些选举的办公室签订了 287(g) 协议，确定了印第安纳州、马里兰州、北卡罗来纳州、威斯康星州和其他地方的选举，其中 ICE 协议在候选人的失败中发挥了作用。今年参选的许多警长都没有遭到反对。但 ICE 协议可能会在两年内再次成为焦点，届时来自佛罗里达州、德克萨斯州和其他拥有大量 287(g) 协议的州的治安官将进行选举。
阿拉曼斯县是共和党的长期据点，拥有近 20 万居民，位于格林斯伯勒和包括罗利、达勒姆和教堂山在内的研究三角都市区之间。随着人口日益多样化，该地区的政治竞争力也随之增强——从 1990 年人口普查中认定为拉美裔的居民为 750 人，增加到 2020 年的近 25,000 人。发言人证实，治安官办公室目前参与了 287(g) 计划，不过去年终止了一项收容 ICE 被拘留者的协议。
约翰逊是白人，于 2002 年首次当选，一直是一位著名且两极分化的人物。他坚称他欢迎合法移民，并否认了持续不断的指控——包括十多年前司法部的一场诉讼，最终以和解告终——即他的办公室对少数族裔居民进行种族歧视。
学校董事会成员塞内卡·罗杰斯说，该县获得了“没有机会阿拉曼斯”的绰号，因为人们认为警察执法不公正，而且黑人和拉丁裔居民缺乏政治代表性。
约翰逊最初在电话中表示，移民政策可能是导致他落败的原因之一。但在后来的一次简短采访中，他表示情况可能并非如此，并指责自己的长期任期以及对共和党人来说残酷的全国政治环境，尤其是在北卡罗来纳州，民主党前州长罗伊·库珀(Roy Cooper)以近20个百分点的优势击败了美国参议院席位。他说，他一直遵守法律并保护公共安全。
活动人士和长期居民表示，拉丁裔社区——在某种程度上，黑人社区——害怕与治安官办公室打交道，并描述了一种感觉，即非白人居民更有可能在交通堵塞后被拦下或拘留。社区组织者莱斯利·阿雷瓦洛 (Leslie Arevalo) 表示，有些人不敢拨打 911，甚至不敢去上班。
选民蕾妮·拉塞尔 (Renee Russell) 表示，治安官与 ICE 的合作给人留下了阿拉曼斯不受欢迎的错误印象。她很高兴看到新的领导层。据当地媒体报道，朗将成为该县第一位黑人警长。
但共和党州参议员艾米·盖利（其选区包括该县）为约翰逊的记录进行了辩护。她说他一直致力于改善培训机会和心理健康服务。尽管盖利不认为移民在竞选中发挥了重要作用，但她想知道其他地方的 ICE 强硬策略是否会加剧人们对更广泛执法部门的担忧。

Democrats have made government contracts one of their top investigative targets, noting that federal money has been flowing to companies linked with Mr. Trump's family, particularly at the Pentagon.

It comes as White House officials have already begun taking steps to exert more control over how agencies and officials respond to congressional requests, anticipating there will be a flood of investigations once Democrats take power in January.

On Monday, White House Counsel Will Scharf told U.S. agencies that they must seek approval from his office and the White House's Office of Legislative Affairs before agreeing to appear before Congress. Scharf also suggested in a recent letter to Rep. Robert Garcia, the top Democrat on the House Oversight Committee, that some congressional investigations may amount to "blatant criminality."

Garcia earlier this week sent letters directing members of Mr. Trump's family and top administration officials to preserve documents. Scharf sought to dismiss the requests, noting in a letter to Democratic lawmakers that they are not yet in the majority and cannot compel compliance.

In a fact sheet, the White House framed the new requirements as "protecting executive privileges from congressional overreach," arguing that some congressional leaders have tried to intrude on executive branch privileges by "harassing private companies that contract with the federal government."

Presidents of both parties have long used executive privilege to resist congressional inquiries, but the claims can set up messy, protracted legal fights as parties dispute whether it applies. Executive privilege allows the president to keep information from the courts, Congress and the public to protect the confidentiality of White House deliberations, but the protection is far from absolute.
Friday's executive order applies to all contractors and subcontractors, a universe of tens of thousands of businesses.

body_zh: 特朗普的新行政命令要求联邦承包商在回应国会之前先与白宫核实 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
根据周五晚间发布的一项新行政命令，特朗普总统指示联邦承包商和分包商就国会提出的询问向其政府进行咨询，并扣留任何白宫认为有特权的通信。
该命令称，这些公司还必须与白宫和美国机构协调，对任何此类请求做出“适当回应”。如果他们不遵守规定，白宫警告他们的合同可能会被终止，并且他们未来与联邦政府的合作可能会暂停。
周五晚间签署的这项命令是政府为抵制民主党在一月份接管国会时预计将采取的广泛而激进的监督努力而采取的最新举措。民主党人已将政府合同作为其首要调查目标之一，并指出联邦资金一直流向与特朗普家族有联系的公司，尤其是五角大楼。
与此同时，白宫官员已经开始采取措施，对各机构和官员如何回应国会要求施加更多控制，预计一旦民主党一月份掌权，将会进行大量调查。
周一，白宫法律顾问威尔·沙夫告诉美国机构，他们在同意出席国会听证会之前必须获得他的办公室和白宫立法事务办公室的批准。沙夫还在最近写给众议院监督委员会民主党领袖罗伯特·加西亚的一封信中表示，一些国会调查可能构成“公然犯罪”。
加西亚本周早些时候致函特朗普家族成员和高级政府官员保存文件。沙夫试图驳回这些要求，并在给民主党议员的一封信中指出，他们尚未占多数，无法强迫他们遵守。
白宫在一份情况说明书中将新要求描述为“保护行政特权免遭国会越权”，并认为一些国会领导人试图通过“骚扰与联邦政府签订合同的私营公司”来侵犯行政部门的特权。
两党总统长期以来一直利用行政特权来抵制国会调查，但由于双方对其是否适用存在争议，这些主张可能会引发混乱、旷日持久的法律斗争。行政特权允许总统向法院、国会和公众保留信息，以保护白宫审议的机密性，但这种保护远非绝对。
周五的行政命令适用于所有承包商和分包商，涵盖数以万计的企业。

title_en: Vance stops short of endorsing Trump’s claim that Iran was close to nuclear weapon
title_zh: 万斯没有支持特朗普关于伊朗接近拥有核武器的说法
summary: US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclea
summary_zh: 美国副总统在白宫新闻发布会上表示，他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但他没有支持特朗普的说法
body_en: US vice-president says it’s not his place to second-guess the president, but refrains from endorsing Trump’s claim

At a White House news conference on Friday, JD Vance stopped short of endorsing Donald Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to obtaining a nuclear weapon in February that it was essential for the US to go to war with the Islamic republic.

In the White House briefing room, Trump was asked about reporting this week that he was unhappy with the US vice-president’s statement blaming Republican losses in the midterm elections on the Iran war.

“I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” Trump said. “I thought the statement was fine, except I would have had one other thing, that if it were asked, I would have said that: ‘Would you do it again?’ And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”

However, Trump’s claim that Iran was so close to developing a nuclear weapon this year that it was necessary to go to war, which he has made dozens of times in the past nine months, is undermined by public evidence and contradicts his own previous statements on US strikes against Iranian facilities in 2025.
At a campaign rally in Alaska last month, Trump insisted that he had to join Israel in attacking Iran in February because, “they were two weeks away from having a nuclear weapon”.

That claim appears at odds with what his then director of national intelligence, Tulsi Gabbard, testified to Congress on 25 March 2025, two months into Trump’s second term: that US intelligence agencies reported that Iran had not tried to make a nuclear weapon for more than two decades. The US intelligence community, Gabbard said, “continues to assess Iran is not building a nuclear weapon and supreme leader Khamenei has not authorized the nuclear weapons program he suspended in 2003”.

Despite that assessment, three months later, on 21 June 2025, Trump ordered the US bombing of Iran’s nuclear enrichment facilities. The strikes, Trump told the public that night , “were a spectacular military success. Iran’s key nuclear enrichment facilities have been completely and totally obliterated.”

Eight months after that, however, when Trump announced the start of a full-scale war on Iran early on 28 February 2026, he said in a video statement from Mar-a-Lago the war was necessary to “ensure that Iran does not obtain a nuclear weapon”.
The morning after this month’s midterm elections, Vance said in a statement posted on social media: “The reason we lost is the war.”

“If you’d like to argue it was worth it, that losing the Senate for the next 6 years was worth it, then do so,” he added. “Argue it was a worthwhile cost to pay. Agree or disagree, that’s at least honest. But everyone knows why we lost.”

In the White House briefing room on Friday, after Trump said that Vance should have said the war was necessary, a reporter asked the vice-president whether he would argue that the war in Iran was worth it.

In his response, Vance said it was not his place to second-guess the president, but refrained from actually endorsing Trump’s claim that the war was essential to stop Iran from creating a nuclear weapon.

“Look, what I’ve said is the goal of keeping Iran from getting a nuclear weapon is absolutely what we need to be doing. It’s the biggest state sponsor of terrorism. If they had a nuclear weapon, they would use it as leverage or, God forbid, they would attack and kill thousands, hundreds of thousands, of innocent people,” Vance said. “I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again.”
“My view is that my goal is, and my job is, to support the president of the United States,” the vice-president said.
The vice president’s office did not respond to a request to comment.
body_zh: 美国副总统表示他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但没有支持特朗普的说法
在周五的白宫新闻发布会上，JD 万斯没有支持唐纳德·特朗普的说法，即伊朗在二月份非常接近获得核武器，以至于美国必须与这个伊斯兰共和国开战。
在白宫简报室，特朗普被问及本周的报道，他对美国副总统将共和党在中期选举中的失败归咎于伊朗战争的声明感到不满。
“我没有说我对此不满意，”特朗普说。 “我认为这个声明很好，除了我还有另一件事，如果有人问我，我会说：‘你会再做一次吗？’绝对，答案是肯定的，因为我们不能允许伊朗拥有核武器。”
然而，特朗普声称伊朗今年已经非常接近研制出核武器，以至于有必要发动战争，而他在过去九个月里已经多次提出这一说法，这一说法被公开证据所推翻，并且与他之前关于美国将于2025年袭击伊朗设施的说法相矛盾。
上个月在阿拉斯加举行的竞选集会上，特朗普坚称他必须在二月份与以色列一起攻击伊朗，因为“他们距离拥有核武器还有两周时间”。
这一说法似乎与时任国家情报总监图尔西·加巴德 (Tulsi Gabbard) 于 2025 年 3 月 25 日（也就是特朗普第二任期两个月后）向国会作证时的说法不一致：美国情报机构报告称，伊朗已有二十多年没有尝试制造核武器。加巴德表示，美国情报界“继续评估伊朗没有制造核武器，最高领袖哈梅内伊也没有授权他在 2003 年暂停的核武器计划”。
尽管有这样的评估，三个月后，即 2025 年 6 月 21 日，特朗普还是下令美国轰炸伊朗的核浓缩设施。特朗普当晚告诉公众，这次袭击“在军事上取得了巨大的成功。伊朗的关键核浓缩设施已被彻底摧毁。”
然而八个月后，当特朗普于 2026 年 2 月 28 日早些时候宣布对伊朗发动全面战争时，他在海湖庄园的视频声明中表示，这场战争对于“确保伊朗不会获得核武器”是必要的。
本月中期选举后的第二天早上，万斯在社交媒体上发布的一份声明中表示：“我们失败的原因是战争。”
“如果你想说这是值得的，认为在未来六年失去参议院是值得的，那就这么做吧，”他补充道。 “认为这是值得付出的代价。无论同意还是不同意，这至少是诚实的。但每个人都知道我们为什么输了。”
周五在白宫新闻发布室，特朗普表示万斯应该表示这场战争是必要的，之后一名记者问副总统是否会认为伊朗战争值得。
万斯在回应中表示，他没有资格对总统进行事后批评，但他没有真正支持特朗普的说法，即这场战争对于阻止伊朗制造核武器至关重要。
“听着，我所说的是，阻止伊朗获得核武器的目标绝对是我们需要做的。它是恐怖主义的最大支持者。如果他们拥有核武器，他们就会用它作为杠杆，否则，上帝保佑，他们会攻击并杀害数千、数十万无辜人民，”万斯说。 “我认为总统是做出决定的人，总统已经说过他会再次这样做。”
“我的观点是，我的目标是，我的工作是支持美国总统，”副总统说。
副总统办公室没有回应置评请求。

title_en: Federal judge denies request to release man shot by immigration agents in New York
title_zh: 联邦法官驳回释放纽约移民局枪杀男子的请求
summary: Oscar Belgal, a Dominican national, was shot by ICE agents as he drove his five-year-old son home from school A federal judge on Friday declined to release from custody a man who was shot and wounded by immigration officers as they arrested him in New York in
summary_zh: 多米尼加国民奥斯卡·贝尔加尔 (Oscar Belgal) 在开车送五岁儿子放学回家时被 ICE 特工开枪射击。周五，联邦法官拒绝重新审理此事。
body_en: Oscar Belgal, a Dominican national, was shot by ICE agents as he drove his five-year-old son home from school
A federal judge on Friday declined to release from custody a man who was shot and wounded by immigration officers as they arrested him in New York in October.

The US district court judge Hector Gonzalez said in a written ruling that agents may have made a procedural error in serving an arrest warrant on Oscar Belgal before he was given a notice to appear in immigration court. However, he wrote, that was merely a technical error that does not require Belgal to be released from federal custody pending deportation proceedings.

Belgal, a 28-year-old Dominican national, entered the US illegally in 2021, and about two years later he was arrested on robbery and other charges and eventually pleaded guilty to grand larceny. He was given a sentence of probation, and in 2025 he was arrested again, this time on allegations that he attempted to sell controlled substances. That case remains pending.
Judge says ICE ‘made a mockery of court orders’ with instant re-arrest policy
On 8 October, amid the Trump administration’s ongoing immigration crackdown, US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents found him as he was driving his five-year-old son home from school.

Security camera footage released by the New York City police shows an officer dressed in plainclothes running up to the car with his gun pointed at Belgal, then immediately using the barrel of his gun to bash in the driver’s side window. A second officer then draws his gun as Belgal pulls out, away from the two officers. The chase ends moments later, with Belgal’s bullet-riddled car coming to rest.
Belgal was struck in the shoulder and neck. His son was not injured. His attorneys said he didn’t learn the men were ICE officers until he awoke later in the hospital.

“It is unconscionable that Mr Belgal should have to endure another day in detention, separated from his family, particularly given everything he has already suffered,” said a written statement from the Legal Aid Society, a non-profit law firm that represents him.

Federal officials maintained that ICE officers fired their weapons because they believed their lives were in danger. They said Belgal smashed his car into two government vehicles and “accelerated toward other officers”.

His attorneys said the agents did not have a valid warrant and never identified themselves before running up to Belgal’s car, smashing a window and firing several shots inside. The lawyers also argued in their filings that Belgal’s due process rights were violated because he was subjected to “unreasonable use of extreme force” during his arrest.

The judge disagreed that the agents did not have a valid warrant. And the petition Belgal filed for release from custody was not an appropriate venue for arguing that the agents used excessive force, he said.
Gonzalez noted that Belgal can still ask the immigration court to release him on bond.
body_zh: 多米尼加国民奥斯卡·贝尔加尔 (Oscar Belgal) 在开车送五岁儿子放学回家时被 ICE 特工开枪射击
周五，一名联邦法官拒绝释放一名 10 月份在纽约被捕时被移民官员开枪打伤的男子。
美国地方法院法官赫克托·冈萨雷斯(Hector Gonzalez)在一份书面裁决中表示，在奥斯卡·贝尔加尔收到出庭通知之前，特工人员在向他发出逮捕令时可能犯了程序错误。然而，他写道，这只是一个技术错误，并不需要在等待驱逐程序期间将贝尔加尔从联邦拘留中释放。
贝尔加是一名 28 岁的多米尼加公民，于 2021 年非法进入美国，大约两年后，他因抢劫等罪名被捕，最终承认犯有重大盗窃罪。他被判处缓刑，并于 2025 年再次被捕，这次是因为他被指控试图出售管制药物。该案仍在审理中。
法官称 ICE 的即时重新逮捕政策“是对法庭命令的嘲弄”
10 月 8 日，在特朗普政府持续镇压移民期间，美国移民和海关执法局 (ICE) 特工在他开车送五岁儿子放学回家时发现了他。
纽约市警方公布的监控录像显示，一名便衣警官跑到车前，用枪指着贝尔加尔，然后立即用枪管猛击驾驶员侧的车窗。当贝尔加尔退出时，第二名警官拔出了枪，远离了两名警官。几分钟后，追逐结束了，贝尔加那辆布满弹孔的汽车停下来。
贝尔加尔的肩膀和颈部被击中。他的儿子没有受伤。他的律师表示，直到他后来在医院醒来后，他才知道这些人是 ICE 官员。
代表贝尔加尔的非营利律师事务所法律援助协会在一份书面声明中表示：“贝尔加尔先生不得不再忍受一天的拘留，与家人分离，这是不合理的，特别是考虑到他已经遭受的一切。”
联邦官员坚称，ICE 官员开枪是因为他们认为自己的生命处于危险之中。他们说，贝尔加尔将他的汽车撞向两辆政府车辆，并“加速冲向其他警察”。
他的律师表示，特工们没有有效的逮捕令，也从未表明自己的身份，然后跑到贝尔加尔的车前，砸碎了车窗，并向车内开了几枪。律师们还在文件中辩称，贝尔加尔的正当程序权利受到侵犯，因为他在被捕期间受到“不合理使用极端武力”。
法官不同意特工没有有效搜查令的说法。他说，贝尔加尔提出的释放羁押请愿书并不是争论特工过度使用武力的适当场所。
冈萨雷斯指出，贝尔加尔仍然可以要求移民法庭保释他。

title_en: USDA, FBI breached by hackers amid spate of tech outages – reports
title_zh: 美国农业部、联邦调查局因一系列技术中断而遭到黑客入侵——报告
summary: Latest intrusions targeted farmer-payment system at the USDA and the FBI’s National Crime Information Center Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the FBI , national media reported on Friday, amid deepening concerns over a spate of tech
summary_zh: 最新的入侵针对美国农业部和联邦调查局国家犯罪信息中心的农民支付系统黑客入侵了美国农业部
body_en: Latest intrusions targeted farmer-payment system at the USDA and the FBI’s National Crime Information Center
Hackers breached the US Department of Agriculture (USDA) and the FBI , national media reported on Friday, amid deepening concerns over a spate of tech outages at key American institutions.
The breaches were first reported by NBC News and CNN respectively, and it remained unclear whether they were related and who was responsible.
Major outages in recent weeks have disrupted travel , communications and e-commerce for countless users across the US, even affecting a top-secret network at the National Security Agency .
FBI investigates breach of jobs website as hackers claim ‘very sensitive data’ stolen
Donald Trump has sought to calm the public, urging people to “relax”. Officials said the various outages were not linked to criminal activity.
The USDA told employees that a system used to facilitate payments to farmers was targeted in a cyber-attack, NBC reported on Friday, citing two former department officials.
The hackers may use the payments system as a back door to access more sensitive material, the former officials told NBC.

The USDA deals with “a bunch of scary biologic issues” and “if an adversary or a competitor were to have access to that same information … they could use our own research against us,” a former official was quoted as saying.
CNN said separately on Friday that the FBI was hacked for the second time since September.
The bureau was investigating an intrusion of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC) by apparent hackers, CNN reported citing two people briefed on the probe.
The NCIC has a nationwide criminal information database linking federal, state and local law enforcement and is used to share information on warrants and background checks.

“Every day, officers across the country rely on NCIC to identify wanted fugitives, check for outstanding warrants, and access information that can directly impact officer and public safety,” a former FBI official told CNN.
The former official expressed concerns that hackers “could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on”.
AFP has asked the FBI and the USDA for comment.
Ironically, the FBI director, Kash Patel, on Thursday appeared on the Fox News show hosted by Sean Hannity to tout measures his agency had implemented to thwart cyber-attacks.
Patel said the FBI and the US intelligence community would continue to “monitor those activities for nefarious actors” through an anti-cyber-attack initiative dubbed Operation Winter Shield.
“And when and if such an actor comes up, you can rest assured that this FBI is going to hunt them down,” Patel said.

The newly uncovered breaches at the FBI and the USDA were described as hacks, which are different from outages such as the ones that afflicted Microsoft Outlook and the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) earlier in November.
body_zh: 最新的入侵针对的是美国农业部和联邦调查局国家犯罪信息中心的农民支付系统
据国家媒体周五报道，黑客入侵了美国农业部 (USDA) 和联邦调查局 (FBI)，人们对美国主要机构发生的一系列技术故障的担忧日益加深。
这些违规行为首先由 NBC 新闻和 CNN 分别报道，目前尚不清楚这些事件是否相关以及责任人是谁。
最近几周的重大停电已经扰乱了美国无数用户的旅行、通信和电子商务，甚至影响了国家安全局的绝密网络。
黑客声称“非常敏感的数据”被盗，联邦调查局正在调查就业网站的违规行为
唐纳德·特朗普试图安抚公众，敦促人们“放松”。官员们表示，各种停电与犯罪活动无关。
据美国全国广播公司 (NBC) 周五援引两名前部门官员的消息报道，美国农业部告诉员工，用于向农民付款的系统成为网络攻击的目标。
前官员告诉 NBC，黑客可能会利用支付系统作为后门来访问更敏感的材料。
一位前官员表示，美国农业部处理“一系列可怕的生物问题”，“如果对手或竞争对手能够获得相同的信息……他们可能会利用我们自己的研究来对付我们”。
美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 周五另外表示，FBI 遭遇自 9 月份以来的第二次黑客攻击。
据美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 援引两名了解调查情况的人士报道，该局正在调查国家犯罪信息中心 (NCIC) 遭明显黑客入侵的事件。
NCIC 拥有一个连接联邦、州和地方执法部门的全国性犯罪信息数据库，用于共享逮捕令和背景调查的信息。
一位前联邦调查局官员告诉 CNN：“全国各地的警官每天都依靠 NCIC 来识别通缉逃犯、检查未执行的逮捕令以及获取可能直接影响警官和公共安全的信息。”
这位前官员表示担心黑客“可能会损害官员所依赖的信息的准确性”。
法新社已要求联邦调查局和美国农业部发表评论。
具有讽刺意味的是，联邦调查局局长卡什·帕特尔周四出现在肖恩·汉尼蒂主持的福克斯新闻节目中，宣传他的机构为阻止网络攻击而采取的措施。
帕特尔表示，联邦调查局和美国情报界将通过一项名为“冬季盾牌行动”的反网络攻击计划，继续“监控不法分子的这些活动”。
“当这样的演员出现时，你可以放心，联邦调查局将会追捕他们，”帕特尔说。
FBI 和 USDA 新发现的漏洞被描述为黑客攻击，这与 11 月初影响 Microsoft Outlook 和联邦航空管理局 (FAA) 的中断不同。

title_en: US pursuit of ‘Trump-class’ warships has blown cost of new fleet by billions, report warns
title_zh: 报告警告说，美国对“特朗普级”战舰的追求使新舰队的成本增加了数十亿美元
summary: Iran war stretching fleet’s capacity, navy chief admits, as CBO finds estimated cost of new ships ‘unrealistically low’ The US navy’s commitment to the new Trump-class battleships has blown out the cost of its new fleet by billions of dollars, a report to the
summary_zh: 海军参谋长承认，伊朗战争扩大了舰队的能力，国会预算办公室发现新舰的估计成本“低得不切实际”
body_en: Iran war stretching fleet’s capacity, navy chief admits, as CBO finds estimated cost of new ships ‘unrealistically low’

The US navy’s commitment to the new Trump-class battleships has blown out the cost of its new fleet by billions of dollars, a report to the US Congress has found, as the acting secretary of the navy conceded this week the Iran war was “stretching” the fleet’s capacity.

The challenges facing the world’s biggest naval force were highlighted this week, when the return of the USS George Washington from the Middle East on Wednesday ended a rare three-month period when the US had no aircraft carrier across all of the Pacific. Deployments have been regularly running beyond 300 days, with the maintenance and repair of ships deferred so they can stay at sea longer.
US army postpones plan to detonate bomb-making chemical amid outcry
Outpaced in shipbuilding by China, the US navy wants to increase its fleet from 286 battle force ships to 381 over the next 30 years.

But the congressional budget office’s analysis of the navy’s 2027 shipbuilding plan states the navy’s projections have underestimated the costs of its new fleet by billions because some ships’ designs have proven more complicated than expected, and the “estimated costs of some ships were unrealistically low in earlier shipbuilding plans”.
Total shipbuilding costs would average $54bn annually (in 2026 dollars) over the next 30 years, the CBO found, about 18% more than navy estimates.

“Much of the additional costs in the 2027 plan stem from the navy’s decision to purchase 15 large, heavily armed battleships, which would concentrate firepower in a few large ships and thus would be at odds with the navy’s stated goal of distributing it among a greater number of ships or vessels.”

The 15 new battleships are the proposed “Trump-class” warships , which the president has said will be 100-times more powerful than any previous warship in a US fleet, and will “inspire fear in America’s enemies all over the world”. Senate appropriators this week proposed cutting to zero the $1bn the navy sought in advanced procurement this fiscal year for the Trump-class ships.
On Wednesday, the acting secretary of the navy, Hung Cao, conceded before a Senate confirmation hearing that the Iran war was “stretching” the fleet’s capacity.
“This war, again, I know it’s a strain on our navy,” he told senators.

His term as acting secretary – he requires a special waiver to be permanently appointed because of his recent active service – was criticised by Democratic senators. “The world is less safe as a result of the Iran war,” Richard Blumenthal told Cao.

“We’ve seen costs soar, lives lost, casualties. Our relationships with allies deteriorate as a result of this war. In fact, the navy has been stretched beyond sustainable limits under your watch, and the fleet is in worse condition than it was when you took office along with this president.”
The conflict in Iran is estimated to have cost the US $260bn, Michigan senator Elissa Slotkin told the committee hearing.
“Yet we do not have the same freedom of navigation that we had a year ago.”

For all of the effort and resourcing of the world’s most powerful bluewater navy to keep the strait of Hormuz open, passage across the contested waters remains at barely more than a third of pre-war levels.

Shipping traffic remains approximately 65% below the rate before the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on 28 February, according to the latest weekly report from the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations .
A year ago, the cost to insure a commercial ship for a single passage through the Strait of Hormuz was $54,000, Cao told the Senate: “Today it’s $64m just to get across.”
The additional cost of every passage is borne by consumers all around the world, in higher prices for fuel, fertilizer, and food.
body_zh: 海军参谋长承认，伊朗战争扩大了舰队的能力，国会预算办公室发现新舰的估计成本“低得不切实际”
提交给美国国会的一份报告发现，美国海军对新型特朗普级战列舰的承诺使其新舰队的成本增加了数十亿美元，美国海军代理部长本周承认，伊朗战争正在“拉伸”舰队的能力。
本周，乔治·华盛顿号航空母舰从中东返回，结束了美国在整个太平洋地区没有航空母舰的罕见的三个月时期，这凸显了世界上最大的海军力量面临的挑战。部署的定期运行时间超过 300 天，船舶的维护和修理也被推迟，以便它们可以在海上停留更长时间。
在强烈抗议下，美国陆军推迟了引爆炸弹化学物质的计划
美国海军在造船方面落后于中国，希望在未来 30 年内将其舰队从 286 艘战舰增加到 381 艘。
但国会预算办公室对海军2027年造船计划的分析指出，海军的预测低估了新舰队的成本数十亿美元，因为事实证明，一些舰艇的设计比预期更复杂，而且“在早期的造船计划中，一些舰艇的估计成本低得不切实际”。
美国国会预算办公室发现，未来 30 年造船总成本平均每年为 540 亿美元（以 2026 年美元计算），比海军的估计高出约 18%。
“2027年计划中的大部分额外成本源于海军决定购买15艘大型全副武装战列舰，这会将火力集中在几艘大型舰艇上，因此与海军将火力分配给更多舰艇的既定目标相矛盾。”
这 15 艘新战舰是拟议中的“特朗普级”战舰，总统表示，这艘战舰的威力将比美国舰队中任何以前的战舰强大 100 倍，并将“激起美国全世界敌人的恐惧”。参议院拨款者本周提议将海军本财年为特朗普级舰艇提前采购的 10 亿美元削减至零。
周三，代理海军部长曹洪在参议院确认听证会上承认，伊朗战争正在“拉伸”舰队的能力。
他对参议员们说：“我知道这场战争再次给我们的海军带来了压力。”
他担任代理国务卿的任期——由于他最近的现役服役，需要特别豁免才能被永久任命——受到了民主党参议员的批评。 “由于伊朗战争，世界变得更加不安全，”理查德·布卢门撒尔告诉曹。
“我们看到成本飙升、生命损失和伤亡。这场战争导致我们与盟友的关系恶化。事实上，在你的领导下，海军已经超出了可持续的限度，舰队的状况比你和这位总统一起上任时更糟糕。”
密歇根州参议员埃丽莎·斯洛特金 (Elissa Slotkin) 在委员会听证会上表示，伊朗冲突估计造成 2600 亿美元损失。
“然而，我们没有一年前那样的航行自由。”
尽管世界上最强大的蓝水海军为保持霍尔木兹海峡的开放付出了所有的努力和资源，但穿过有争议水域的通行能力仍仅略高于战前水平的三分之一。
根据英国海事贸易运营部最新的每周报告，航运量仍比 2 月 28 日美国和以色列对伊朗发动袭击之前的水平低约 65%。
一年前，一艘商船通过霍尔木兹海峡的保险费用为 54,000 美元，曹告诉参议院：“如今，仅通过霍尔木兹海峡就需要 6400 万美元。”
每一次航行的额外成本都由世界各地的消费者承担，燃料、化肥和食品的价格上涨。

title_en: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history
title_zh: 政治周：特朗普从亚洲归来；称赞这次旅行是历史上最好的旅行之一
summary: President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统结束亚洲之行，称这是对该大陆或其他任何地方最成功的总统访问之一。
body_en: Week in Politics: Trump returns from Asia; hails trip as one of best in history President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent -- or anywhere else -- in American history.
President Trump returned from his trip to Asia, saying it was one of the most successful presidential visits to that continent — or anywhere else — in American history.

In China, this week, President Trump attended the first-ever trilateral meeting with the leaders of China and Russia. Some commentators compared it to the 1945 Yalta Conference, where post-war leaders divided Eastern Europe.

PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: I didn't go having us talk about Yalta, and if you look, Winston Churchill, Stalin, FDR - which was a big one - I didn't think about it. I just went saying, I get along great with these two people. We'll work out our differences. We've been able to work them out. And all of a sudden, I see you people talking it's the biggest but - and then I realized how big it was. It was an amazing event.
SIMON: President Trump during an hour-and-a-half-long press conference yesterday at the White House. NPR Senior contributor Ron Elving joins us. Ron, thanks so much for being with us.
RON ELVING, BYLINE: Good to be with you, Scott.
SIMON: What do you make of this meeting, President Trump with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin all seated around a big round table?

ELVING: Yes, an enormous circular table - to some degree, a symbol of equality among the three men, but still staged to place Chinese President Xi as host. We know that President Trump cares a lot about visuals and staging, and here we had perhaps the most elaborate photo opportunity in history. If you watched the news conference yesterday as a Trump admirer, you got plenty to feed that. Otherwise, you could have felt the claims of peacemaking and dealmaking in Asia were long on promise and woefully short on details.

When asked yesterday whether his friend Putin was a friend to America, Trump said he could not speak to America, a remarkable thing for a president to say. Then he went back to when Putin denied colluding with Trump's first campaign in 2016, saying how much he had appreciated Putin's support in that episode. Ukraine's leader, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, responded last night several hours later, saying for Ukraine, Putin was not a friend, but a killer using terrorism against civilians.
SIMON: Ron, any appearances aside, does a meeting like this have consequences - real-world consequences?

ELVING: It could have if these various vows of peaceful cooperation bear fruit, or if these vaunted trade deals come to pass. But what we do know at this point is that Russia this week launched one of its most massive assaults against Ukraine since it first invaded that country in 2022, assaults against civilian targets that also struck Poland, a NATO ally of the U.S. And it makes a difference that Trump was more interested in meeting with Chinese President Xi than he was in confronting that country's efforts to obtain the most advanced American computer chips.
SIMON: On a question about the Democrats, Hakeem Jeffries on track to be speaker of the House in January. On the Senate side, Senator Chuck Schumer faces a challenge. What are you watching for?

ELVING: Jeffries is now the official Democratic nominee. He got 251 votes out of 262 cast - way more than he'll need to be formally elected in January. The last time, when Nancy Pelosi was nominated for speaker, she barely got over 200 votes and had to do some heavy lifting to bring her dissidents on board. Jeffries, from the start, can concentrate on Trump and the Republicans from a secure position.

Now, the Democrats in the Senate have yet to vote, and the presumed leader there - another New Yorker, Chuck Schumer - has a long history in leadership and perhaps too much baggage for younger Democrats. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has challenged him and promises a fresh face. But so far, if there's a big move to Van Hollen happening among Senate Democrats, it remains below the surface.
SIMON: And finally, Elon Musk - richest person in the world, biggest spender of the midterms - now says he's not MAGA.

ELVING: Yes. You may recall his red ball cap that said Trump was right about everything. So maybe not so right about Elon Musk. His promise to cut trillions from the federal budget fizzled. Then he dropped something approaching half a billion dollars on the midterms and got shut out. He is a brilliant engineer and businessman, to be sure, but that does not always translate to success in politics. Republicans won't miss him on the campaign trail if he's really through with it, but they may well miss that money.

body_zh: 政治周：特朗普从亚洲归来；特朗普总统从亚洲之行归来，称赞这是历史上最好的访问之一，称这是美国历史上对该大陆或其他任何地方最成功的总统访问之一。
特朗普总统结束亚洲之行后表示，这是美国历史上对该大陆或其他任何地方最成功的总统访问之一。
本周，特朗普总统在中国出席了与中国和俄罗斯领导人的首次三边会议。一些评论家将其与 1945 年雅尔塔会议进行了比较，当时战后领导人分裂了东欧。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：我没有让我们谈论雅尔塔，如果你看的话，温斯顿·丘吉尔、斯大林、罗斯福——这是一件大事——我没有想到这一点。我只是说，我和这两个人相处得很好。我们会解决我们的分歧。我们已经能够解决它们。突然之间，我看到你们说这是最大的，但是 - 然后我意识到它有多大。这是一个了不起的事件。
西蒙：特朗普总统昨天在白宫举行了一个半小时的新闻发布会。 NPR 高级撰稿人 Ron Elving 加入我们。罗恩，非常感谢你和我们在一起。
罗恩·埃尔文连线：很高兴和你在一起，斯科特。
西蒙：特朗普总统与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京坐在一张大圆桌旁，你对这次会议有何看法？
埃尔文：是的，一张巨大的圆桌——在某种程度上，这是三个人之间平等的象征，但仍然是为了让中国国家主席习近平担任东道主。我们知道特朗普总统非常关心视觉效果和舞台布置，在这里我们可能有历史上最精致的拍照机会。如果你作为特朗普的崇拜者观看了昨天的新闻发布会，你会得到足够的满足。否则，你可能会觉得关于在亚洲缔造和平和达成交易的说法是空洞的承诺，而令人遗憾的是缺乏细节。
昨天，当被问及他的朋友普京是否是美国的朋友时，特朗普表示他无法与美国交谈，这对于一位总统来说是一件了不起的事情。然后他回到了普京否认与特朗普2016年第一次竞选活动勾结的情况，并表示他非常感谢普京在那一集的支持。乌克兰领导人弗拉基米尔·泽连斯基昨晚几小时后做出回应，称对于乌克兰来说，普京不是朋友，而是对平民使用恐怖主义的杀手。
西蒙：罗恩，抛开外表不谈，像这样的会议会产生后果吗——现实世界的后果？
埃尔文：如果这些和平合作的各种誓言能够取得成果，或者如果这些吹嘘的贸易协议得以实现，那就可能实现。但我们目前所知道的是，俄罗斯本周对乌克兰发动了自2022年首次入侵乌克兰以来最大规模的袭击之一，对平民目标的袭击也袭击了美国的北约盟友波兰。而特朗普更感兴趣的是与中国国家主席习近平会面，而不是对抗该国获取最先进的美国计算机芯片的努力。
西蒙：关于民主党的问题，哈基姆·杰弗里斯有望在一月份担任众议院议长。在参议院方面，参议员查克·舒默面临着挑战。你在看什么？
埃尔文：杰弗里斯现在是民主党的正式提名人。他在 262 名选民中获得了 251 票——远远超过了他在一月份正式当选所需的票数。上次南希·佩洛西被提名为议长时，她仅仅获得了 200 多张选票，并且不得不做一些繁重的工作来让持不同政见者加入。杰弗里斯从一开始就可以在安全的位置上专注于特朗普和共和党。
现在，参议院的民主党人尚未投票，而参议院的假定领导人——另一位纽约人查克·舒默(Chuck Schumer)——有着悠久的领导历史，对年轻的民主党人来说也许有太多的包袱。马里兰州的克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 向他发起了挑战，并承诺将带来一张新面孔。但到目前为止，即使参议院民主党人对范霍伦有重大举动，也仍处于表面之下。
西蒙：最后，埃隆·马斯克 - 世界上最富有的人，中期选举中最大的花钱者 - 现在说他不是 MAGA。
埃尔文：是的。你可能还记得他的红色球帽，上面写着特朗普在一切事情上都是对的。所以埃隆·马斯克的说法也许不太正确。他从联邦预算中削减数万亿美元的承诺落空了。然后他在中期选举中输掉了接近 5 亿美元的资金并被拒之门外。诚然，他是一位出色的工程师和商人，但这并不总是意味着政治上的成功。如果他真的结束了竞选活动，共和党人就不会在竞选过程中怀念他，但他们很可能会怀念这笔钱。

title_en: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran
title_zh: 特朗普表示他希望与伊朗达成“永久”协议
summary: Despite rising tension, President Trump told an Israeli outlet he may not make a decision on his next move in the Iran war until 2027.
summary_zh: 尽管紧张局势加剧，特朗普总统对一家以色列媒体表示，他可能要到 2027 年才能就伊朗战争的下一步行动做出决定。
body_en: Live Updates: Trump says he wants "permanent" deal with Iran; warns next move may not come until 2027

President Trump told an Israeli TV network on Thursday that he is "not rushing" and could wait until 2027 to make a decision on his next move in the war with Iran . He told Fox News on Saturday that he wants a "permanent" deal with the regime.

Despite Mr. Trump's remark, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News Israel and the U.S. are considering launching a new assault on Iran in the short term, with the Netanyahu administration concerned about how rapidly Iran is rebuilding its weapons production capacity.

Iran on Thursday rejected Mr. Trump's accusation that it may be seeking to develop chemical or biological weapons, with the foreign ministry saying U.S. allegations "keep changing" and are following "the same fraudulent script" as the justification for the 2003 U.S. invasion of Iraq.
8:34 PM Athlete swims Strait of Hormuz to raise awareness of Iran war's toll on wildlife

British endurance swimmer Lewis Pugh has swum in the North Pole and Antarctica to draw attention to environmental causes. But battling freezing waters and extreme conditions hasn't prepared him for his latest challenge: swimming the Strait of Hormuz while tankers are attacked and blown up nearby.
Pugh, who is a United Nations Patron of the Oceans, spent three days this week swimming parts of the dangerous waterway to highlight how the war with Iran threatens the area's habitat and wildlife.

Wearing only swimming trunks, goggles and a cap bearing the U.N. logo, the athlete started from the Musandam Peninsula, on the southern tip of the strait, and ended by rounding the Cape of Hormuz, completing about 9.3 miles in total. Pugh is believed to be the first person to undertake a long-distance swim there since the war started.
The swimmer said that minutes after he entered the water on Monday, he heard two loud explosions that rocked the sea.

title_en: ‘Grandfather’ or ‘godfather’? Republicans know they’re stuck with Trump
title_zh: “祖父”还是“干爹”？共和党人知道他们被特朗普困住了
summary: Some grassroots GOP leaders want Trump to stay out of 2028 — even though they know he won’t.
summary_zh: 一些草根共和党领导人希望特朗普远离 2028 年——尽管他们知道他不会。
body_en: Republican leaders grappling with how to recover after their devastating midterm losses agree on one thing: President Donald Trump isn't going anywhere in 2028, even if some wish he would.

Interviews with more than two dozen GOP state and county officials from red, blue and purple states across the country conducted since Election Day revealed a party still processing their election drubbing and at a loss for how to move forward. Some want to move on from Trump entirely. Some are eager for his involvement. And others are just resigned that he’s going to do whatever he wants, regardless of their preferences.

All of them are worried about the party’s chances of retaining control of the White House in two short years, but they also recognize its current occupant is going to continue to exercise a huge role in the future of the party.

“President Trump is going to be part of it, whether we want that or not,” said Arkansas GOP chair Joseph Wood. “His voters are still going to be Republicans that we need to have come out in this election in two years.”

That leaves the party in a precarious position. A recent Reuters/Ipsos poll found the president’s approval rating at 32% overall, and at 70% among Republicans — down from 91% on inauguration day last year. A POLITICO Poll taken after the midterms found 56% of Trump’s 2024 voters believe the Republican Party needs to distance itself from him and his agenda. But no one in the party expects that to happen. And Trump has already taken steps to maintain his grip on the GOP, endorsing Republican National Committee Chair Joe Gruters for another term and ordering his powerful super PAC to continue fundraising ahead of 2028.
A handful of Republican grassroots leaders were openly critical of Trump.
“I don't know how much he really has to offer,” said Vermont GOP chair Paul Dame. “I think most people are ready to move on in a new direction.”
Added Michael Bub, the chair of ruby-red Taylor County, Wisconsin, Republican Party :“He should stay out of it. Look at the people he endorsed: They lost.”
In a statement, RNC spokesperson Natalie Baldassare said “President Trump remains the unequivocal leader of our party.”

“Republicans will continue to harness his ability to energize our voters and expose the Democrats' disastrous record to win in 2028,” she said. The White House demurred, pointing to the RNC’s response.
Many party officials are resigned to Trump doing whatever he wants, given his domineering personality and strong sway over the party base.
Nebraska Republican Party Chair Mary Jane Truemper said “Donald Trump's going to play whatever role he wants to play.”
“He's the president,” Truemper said. “I look at things as they are and not as I want them to be.”
That’s leaving some state-level Republican leaders wanting the president to take on a more constructive role and be willing to let other candidates and ideas rise.

“I hope he becomes kind of the mentor grandfather, and not the godfather,” said Kansas GOP chair Danedri Herbert. “In America, we hope and expect our presidents to not keep a tight grip on the party, to recognize that now it's time for me to mentor the next generation.”

Added outgoing Minnesota Republican Party Chair Alex Plechash: “We need to capitalize on what he brought to the party and do what we can to retain that. But there has been a definite turn in the political landscape.”
Virtually every GOP official cited the poor political environment caused in part by the president’s handling of the economy and the war in Iran as the reason for the party’s midterm meltdown.
But many stopped short of laying the blame directly at the president’s feet, a sign of how criticism of Trump is still verboten within the party.
“I don't want to play the blame game, because I just don't think it's productive,” said West Virginia GOP chair Josh Holstein. “But I do think that it was more economics than it was anything.”

Many GOP chairs praised the president’s ability to bring in new voters to the party and credited him for working to turn those voters out on behalf of other candidates. Still, some said they hope Trump’s generation-defining tenure at the top of the party comes to an end, allowing Republicans to choose the nominee without his influence.
body_zh: 正在努力解决中期选举惨败后如何恢复的共和党领导人一致同意一件事：唐纳德·特朗普总统在 2028 年不会去任何地方，即使有些人希望他这么做。
自选举日以来对来自全国红州、蓝州和紫州的两打共和党州和县官员进行的采访显示，该党仍在处理选举惨败的情况，并且不知道如何继续前进。有些人希望完全摆脱特朗普。有些人渴望他的参与。而其他人则只能听天由命，认为他会做任何他想做的事，不管他们的喜好如何。
他们所有人都担心该党在短短两年内保住白宫控制权的机会，但他们也认识到现任白宫主人将继续在该党的未来中发挥巨大作用。
阿肯色州共和党主席约瑟夫·伍德表示：“无论我们是否愿意，特朗普总统都将参与其中。” “他的选民仍然是共和党人，我们需要在两年后的这次选举中站出来。”

这使得该党处于岌岌可危的境地。路透社/益普索最近的一项民意调查显示，总统的整体支持率为 32%，共和党人的支持率为 70%，低于去年就职当天的 91%。中期选举后进行的一项政治民意调查显示，2024 年特朗普的选民中有 56% 认为共和党需要与他和他的议程保持距离。但党内没有人预计这种情况会发生。特朗普已经采取措施维持对共和党的控制，支持共和党全国委员会主席乔·格鲁特斯连任，并命令其强大的超级政治行动委员会在 2028 年之前继续筹款。
一些共和党基层领导人公开批评特朗普。
“我不知道他到底能提供多少，”佛蒙特州共和党主席保罗·戴姆 (Paul Dame) 说。 “我认为大多数人已经准备好朝着新的方向前进。”
威斯康星州红宝石泰勒县共和党主席迈克尔·布布补充道：“他应该置身事外。看看他支持的人：他们输了。”
共和党全国委员会发言人娜塔莉·巴尔达萨雷在一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统仍然是我们党明确的领导人。”
“共和党人将继续利用他的能力来激励我们的选民并揭露民主党的灾难性记录，以便在 2028 年获胜，”她说。白宫对此表示反对，并指出了共和党全国委员会的回应。
鉴于特朗普的霸道个性和对党内基础的强大影响力，许多党内官员已经听任特朗普为所欲为。
内布拉斯加州共和党主席玛丽·简·特鲁姆珀表示：“唐纳德·特朗普将扮演他想扮演的任何角色。”
“他是总统，”特鲁姆珀说。 “I look at things as they are and not as I want them to be.”
这使得一些州级共和党领导人希望总统发挥更具建设性的作用，并愿意让其他候选人和想法崛起。
堪萨斯州共和党主席丹德里·赫伯特说：“我希望他成为祖父的导师，而不是教父。” “在美国，我们希望并期望我们的总统不要对党保持严格控制，要认识到现在是我指导下一代的时候了。”
即将离任的明尼苏达州共和党主席亚历克斯·普莱查什补充道：“我们需要利用他给党带来的东西，并尽我们所能来保留这一点。但政治格局已经发生了明显的转变。”
几乎每一位共和党官员都将总统处理经济和伊朗战争造成的恶劣政治环境视为该党中期崩溃的原因。
但许多人并没有直接将责任归咎于总统，这表明党内仍然禁止批评特朗普。
“我不想玩指责游戏，因为我认为这没有成效，”西弗吉尼亚州共和党主席乔什·霍尔斯坦说。 “但我确实认为这更多的是出于经济考虑。”
许多共和党主席赞扬总统为党带来新选民的能力，并赞扬他为其他候选人驱逐这些选民所做的努力。尽管如此，一些人表示，他们希望特朗普在党内高层的决定性任期能够结束，让共和党人能够在不受他影响的情况下选择提名人。

title_en: Race to lead Senate Democrats the latest battlefield in party’s tussle over Israel
title_zh: 领导参议院民主党人的竞赛是该党在以色列问题上争夺的最新战场
summary: Chris Van Hollen and Chuck Schumer represent conflicting visions on issue that has become ‘litmus test’ for Democratic voters The race to lead the Democratic Party’s incoming Senate majority has become the latest battlefield between two conflicting visions for
summary_zh: 克里斯·范·霍伦 (Chris Van Hollen) 和查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 在这个问题上代表了相互矛盾的观点，这一问题已成为民主党选民的“试金石”
body_en: Chris Van Hollen and Chuck Schumer represent conflicting visions on issue that has become ‘litmus test’ for Democratic voters

T he race to lead the Democratic Party’s incoming Senate majority has become the latest battlefield between two conflicting visions for how the US should relate to Israel – a once unquestioned ally whose collapsing standing among the US public has become a defining feature of American politics.

Chuck Schumer, the veteran New York Senator and current Democratic minority leader, is one of Israel’s most reliable supporters in Congress. As he views it, according to an interview he gave last year, his “job” is to “keep the left pro-Israel”.

On the other side is Chris Van Hollen , the Maryland senator and challenger to Schumer for Senate leadership, who in recent years emerged as a steadfast advocate for Palestinian rights in the Senate. He supports sanctions, voted to block sales of weapons to Israel, and advocates for the families of US citizens killed by Israeli soldiers and settlers, as well as against the detention of Palestinian children by the Israeli military.

The two represent two opposing sides of the Democratic party’s approach to Israel at a time when a majority of Democrats hold unfavorable views of it. Van Hollen has repeatedly visited the occupied West Bank. In January 2024 he traveled with Oregon’s senator Jeff Merkley to the Rafah border crossing between Egypt and Gaza, where they denounced Israel’s restrictions on humanitarian aid.

While he has in recent years criticized Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and called him a “major obstacle” to peace, Schumer has been an unflinching supporter of Israel throughout his political career, repeatedly referring to himself as “Shomer Yisrael” or “guardian of Israel”. Earlier this year, he said he views it as part of his job to fight for “all the aid that Israel needs”.

He has opposed the Iran nuclear deal, the boycott, divestment and sanctions movement, and a UN resolution affirming that Israeli settlements in occupied territory are illegal, and supported the US Embassy move to Jerusalem. During the war in Gaza, he has repeatedly voted against measures seeking to restrict military aid and weapons sales to Israel. He did, however, vote in favor of a failed resolution that would have required the state department to produce a report on Israeli human rights abuses in the West Bank, and has supported efforts to impose sanctions on individual settlers.

Schumer’s office did not respond to a request for comment. In a statement, Van Hollen’s office said that “the Israeli government has become increasingly hardline in its approach, diminishing the possibility of a two-state solution, including through its indiscriminate attacks on Gaza and its complicity in the escalating violence in the West Bank”.
“The senator has urged the United States to use its leverage to push the government of Israel to comply with US policy and law.”

While the Senate leader has ample discretion to set the party’s legislative priorities and move bills to the floor for votes, he would not necessarily be able to influence the outcome of specific votes – or foreign policy – especially for the remainder of Trump’s term.

Van Hollen has stressed that his challenge to Schumer is about delivering the “change from the status quo” that drove historic numbers of US voters to elect Democrats earlier this month. He has suggested he has the votes of 15 colleagues, but so far, only five have publicly pledged to back him including Michigan’s newly elected Abdul El-Sayed, an outspoken critic of Israel, Merkley, Vermont’s Bernie Sanders, Minnesota’s Peggy Flanagan and Michigan’s Elissa Slotkin. Several others have criticized Schumer and called for change but not committed to a vote.

While he is clearly the underdog in the race, Van Hollen insists he has a “path” to win. Whether or not he succeeds in his bid to oust Schumer, the race has significantly raised his national profile as an advocate for Palestinian rights.

Outside the Senate, advocacy groups’ endorsements are largely following divides on Israel. Bend the Arc, a progressive Jewish group, noted that “the midterm elections proved that a majority of Americans are hungry for change and American Jews are no exception”. The Institute for Middle Eastern Understanding’s Policy Project cited Schumer’s record as the only current Democratic senator to vote against the Iran nuclear deal as “paving the way” for the current war in Iran.

“Senator Van Hollen is committed to rights-respecting policy and understands that accountability is necessary to comprehensively challenge impunity,” said Brad Parker, associate director of policy at the Center for Constitutional Rights.
“The recent electoral lesson over the past year is that incumbents who ignore the overwhelming and shifting electorate demands to end US complicity in Israeli crimes operate at their own peril.”

Last week, dozens of protesters with the Sunrise Movement, a youth climate organization, were arrested outside Schumer’s Washington office, where they called on the senator to “step up or step aside”.

But Schumer – a titan of the party and the highest-ranking Jewish elected official in US history – has much of the political establishment behind him. He also has the backing of major pro-Israel groups.

“Jewish Americans have been a critical component of a winning Democratic coalition, including in the 2026 midterms,” said Halie Soifer, the Jewish Democratic Council of America’s CEO, which endorsed him. “We’re confident that he’ll lead Democrats to deliver for the American people in a way that is consistent with the values of the Jewish community in the 120th Congress.”
On election night, before Van Hollen announced his challenge, Aipac also issued a statement congratulating Schumer and incoming House speaker Hakeem Jeffries for their caucuses’ wins.
body_zh: 克里斯·范·霍伦和查克·舒默在这个问题上代表了相互矛盾的观点，这一问题已成为民主党选民的“试金石”
民主党即将在参议院获得多数席位的领导权之争已成为美国应如何与以色列打交道的两种相互冲突的愿景之间的最新战场。以色列是一个曾经无可争议的盟友，但其在美国公众中的地位的崩溃已成为美国政治的一个决定性特征。
纽约资深参议员、现任民主党少数党领袖查克·舒默 (Chuck Schumer) 是以色列在国会最可靠的支持者之一。在他看来，根据他去年接受的采访，他的“工作”是“让左翼亲以色列”。
另一边是马里兰州参议员克里斯·范霍伦(Chris Van Hollen)，他是舒默参议院领导权的挑战者，近年来他成为参议院巴勒斯坦权利的坚定倡导者。他支持制裁，投票阻止向以色列出售武器，并为被以色列士兵和定居者杀害的美国公民的家人辩护，并反对以色列军队拘留巴勒斯坦儿童。
在大多数民主党人对以色列持不利看法之际，两人代表了民主党对以色列态度的两个对立面。范霍伦多次访问被占领的约旦河西岸。 2024 年 1 月，他与俄勒冈州参议员杰夫·默克利 (Jeff Merkley) 一起前往埃及和加沙之间的拉法过境点，在那里他们谴责以色列对人道主义援助的限制。
尽管舒默近年来批评以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡并称其为和平的“主要障碍”，但舒默在其整个政治生涯中一直是以色列坚定的支持者，多次称自己为“Shomer Yisrael”或“以色列的守护者”。今年早些时候，他表示，他认为争取“以色列需要的所有援助”是他工作的一部分。
他反对伊朗核协议、抵制、撤资和制裁运动，以及确认以色列在被占领土上的定居点非法的联合国决议，并支持美国大使馆迁往耶路撒冷。在加沙战争期间，他多次投票反对旨在限制对以色列军事援助和武器销售的措施。然而，他确实投票支持了一项失败的决议，该决议要求国务院就以色列在约旦河西岸的侵犯人权行为提交一份报告，并支持对个别定居者实施制裁的努力。
舒默办公室没有回应置评请求。范霍伦办公室在一份声明中表示，“以色列政府的做法变得越来越强硬，削弱了两国解决方案的可能性，包括对加沙的不分青红皂白的袭击以及与约旦河西岸不断升级的暴力事件的共谋”。
“参议员敦促美国利用其影响力推动以色列政府遵守美国的政策和法律。”
尽管参议院领袖拥有足够的自由裁量权来确定该党的立法优先事项并将法案提交表决，但他不一定能够影响具体投票的结果或外交政策，尤其是在特朗普剩余任期内。
范霍伦强调，他对舒默的挑战是实现“改变现状”，推动本月早些时候创下历史新高的美国选民投票给民主党。他表示自己拥有 15 名同事的选票，但到目前为止，只有 5 人公开承诺支持他，其中包括密歇根州新当选的阿卜杜勒·赛义德、以色列的直言不讳的批评者、默克利、佛蒙特州的伯尼·桑德斯、明尼苏达州的佩吉·弗拉纳根和密歇根州的埃丽莎·斯洛特金。其他几人批评舒默并呼吁变革，但没有承诺投票。
虽然范霍伦显然在这场比赛中处于劣势，但他坚称自己有一条获胜的“道路”。无论他是否成功推翻舒默，这场竞选都极大地提升了他作为巴勒斯坦权利倡导者的全国形象。
在参议院之外，倡导团体的支持主要是因为对以色列存在分歧。进步犹太组织 Bend the Arc 指出，“中期选举证明，大多数美国人渴望变革，美国犹太人也不例外”。中东理解研究所的政策项目援引舒默作为唯一投票反对伊朗核协议的现任民主党参议员的记录，称其为当前的伊朗战争“铺平了道路”。
宪法权利中心政策副主任布拉德·帕克表示：“范霍伦参议员致力于尊重权利的政策，并理解问责对于全面挑战有罪不罚现象是必要的。”
“过去一年的选举教训是，如果现任者无视选民要求结束美国与以色列犯罪共谋的压倒性且不断变化的要求，他们就会自食其果。”
上周，青年气候组织“日出运动”的数十名抗议者在舒默华盛顿办公室外被捕，他们呼吁参议员“站出来或让位”。
但舒默——党内的巨头和美国历史上级别最高的犹太民选官员——背后有很多政治建制派的支持。他还得到了主要亲以色列团体的支持。
“犹太裔美国人一直是民主党获胜联盟的重要组成部分，包括在 2026 年中期选举中，”支持他的美国犹太民主委员会首席执行官海莉·索弗 (Halie Soifer) 表示。 “我们相信他将领导民主党以符合第 120 届国会犹太社区价值观的方式为美国人民做出贡献。”
选举之夜，在范·霍伦宣布挑战之前，Aipac 还发表声明，祝贺舒默和即将上任的众议院议长哈基姆·杰弗里斯在党团会议中取得胜利。

title_en: Abdul El-Sayed catches president’s attention with pitch for ‘Trumpcare’
title_zh: 阿卜杜勒·赛义德因宣传“特朗普医改”而引起总统的注意
summary: President Donald Trump responded on Saturday to Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s push for universal healthcare after the progressive Michigan Democrat pitched that it be called “Trumpcare.”
summary_zh: 唐纳德·特朗普总统周六对当选参议员阿卜杜勒·赛义德在进步的密歇根州民主党辩论后推动全民医疗保健做出了回应
body_en: Abdul El-Sayed catches Trump’s attention with pitch for ‘Trumpcare’
President Donald Trump responded on Saturday to Sen.-elect Abdul El-Sayed’s push for universal healthcare after the progressive Michigan Democrat pitched that it be called “Trumpcare.”
“Donald, this is on the table,” El-Sayed wrote in a post on X last week. “Guarantee healthcare for every American, from cradle to grave.”

El-Sayed, a former public health official who made Medicare for All a cornerstone of his campaign, included mock images of “Trumpcare” cards in the post. The cards are branded with the title named after the president and are golden, an homage to Trump’s favorite color.
Trump reposted a screenshot of El-Sayed’s post on Truth Social Saturday, though he didn’t include any text with it.
However, he said in a phone interview with Fox News earlier in the day that he believes the government could “do tremendous things on healthcare” after Democrats take control of Congress in January.

“They have some good points on healthcare, and they have some bad points, and we have some good things, and probably they would say we have some bad things,” Trump said, referring to congressional Democrats. “But there’s a chance we could get great healthcare and a lot of other things, and we do it in a bipartisan way.”
Trump also told reporters at a press conference Friday that he is “open to great healthcare.”

“There’s a real possibility that we get a lot of great things done, especially on healthcare,” he said. “It can be a combination of what we all want, and we could end up with great healthcare in our country. We could end up better than dealing with the Republicans.”
Despite touting his openness to work with Democrats, Trump has also repeatedly emphasized his power to veto legislation since Republican losses in the midterms.
“I’ll get along, probably, with the Democrats unless they want to be destructive,” Trump said the day after the election. “But I have the power of the veto.”

Trump did say in the interview with Fox News on Saturday that he does not think that vetoing “everything” passed by Democrats for the next two years is the way to go. But he also posted another image of himself on Truth Social later in the day, showing him in a red “VETO”-branded hat and a matching jacket.
In a statement Saturday afternoon, El-Sayed said he is “happy to chat” with the president if his intentions to work together on healthcare are genuine.

“If the President is serious about meeting the unmet promise of guaranteed healthcare in this country, I’m ready to work alongside leaders in the Senate like Senators Van Hollen, Sanders, Wyden, and Warren to deliver,” El-Sayed said. “President Trump, give me a call.”
Kyla Guilfoil is a breaking news reporter on the politics team for NBC News Digital.
body_zh: 阿卜杜勒·赛义德因宣传“特朗普医改”而引起特朗普的注意
周六，唐纳德·特朗普总统对当选参议员阿卜杜勒·赛义德推动的全民医疗保健做出了回应，此前这位进步的密歇根州民主党人提出将其称为“特朗普医保”。
“唐纳德，这已经摆在桌面上了，”埃尔-赛义德上周在 X 上的一篇帖子中写道。 “保证每个美国人从摇篮到坟墓的医疗保健。”
前公共卫生官员埃尔-赛义德将全民医疗保险作为其竞选活动的基石，他在帖子中添加了“特朗普医保”卡片的模拟图片。这些卡片上印有以总统命名的头衔，呈金色，向特朗普最喜欢的颜色致敬。
特朗普周六在“真相社交”网站上转发了埃尔-赛义德帖子的屏幕截图，不过他没有在其中添加任何文字。
然而，他在当天早些时候接受福克斯新闻的电话采访时表示，他相信在民主党一月份控制国会后，政府可以“在医疗保健方面做出巨大的事情”。
特朗普在谈到国会民主党人时表示：“他们在医疗保健方面有一些优点，也有一些缺点，而我们有一些优点，但他们可能会说我们有一些缺点。” “但我们有机会获得良好的医疗保健和许多其他东西，而且我们以两党合作的方式做到这一点。”
特朗普还在周五的新闻发布会上告诉记者，他“对优质医疗保健持开放态度”。
“我们确实有可能完成很多伟大的事情，特别是在医疗保健方面，”他说。 “这可以是我们所有人想要的结合，我们最终可以在我们的国家获得良好的医疗保健。我们最终可能比与共和党人打交道更好。”
尽管特朗普宣扬与民主党合作的开放态度，但自从共和党在中期选举中失利后，他也一再强调他拥有否决立法的权力。
“我可能会与民主党相处融洽，除非他们想具有破坏性，”特朗普在大选后的第二天表示。 “但我有否决权。”
特朗普在周六接受福克斯新闻采访时确实表示，他认为否决民主党未来两年通过的“一切”并不是正确的出路。但当天晚些时候，他还在 Truth Social 上发布了另一张自己的照片，照片中他戴着红色的“VETO”品牌帽子和配套的夹克。
埃尔-赛义德在周六下午的一份声明中表示，如果总统在医疗保健方面合作的意图是真诚的，他“很高兴与总统交谈”。
埃尔-赛义德说：“如果总统认真履行这个国家未兑现的医疗保障承诺，我准备与参议员范·霍伦、桑德斯、怀登和沃伦等参议院领导人一起努力实现这一目标。” “特朗普总统，给我打电话。”
Kyla Guilfoil 是 NBC News Digital 政治团队的突发新闻记者。

title_en: Violence breaks out in Mexico after capture of drug kingpin wanted by FBI
title_zh: 联邦调查局通缉毒枭被捕后墨西哥爆发暴力事件
summary: Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores is allegedly the leader of a cartel responsible for drug distribution and importation.
summary_zh: 据称，Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores 是负责毒品分销和进口的贩毒集团的头目。
body_en: Mexico arrests drug kingpin on FBI's 10 Most Wanted, sparking violence in Sinaloa - CBS News

Mexico's military announced Saturday that it had captured a drug kingpin on the Federal Bureau of Investigation's Top 10 Most Wanted List. Violence broke out in the state of Sinaloa afterwards, rattling civilians.

Fausto Isidro Meza-Flores, also known as "El Chapo Isidro," is allegedly the leader of the Meza-Flores Transnational Criminal Organization, which the FBI described as a "heavily armed, major drug-trafficking organization" based in Sinaloa.

The cartel is allegedly responsible for the possession, distribution and importation of heroin, methamphetamine, cocaine, fentanyl and marijuana into the U.S., according to the FBI, and has controlled drug production, transportation and distribution throughout Mexico.

Meza-Flores, his second-in-command "Germán" and cartel financial operator "José N" were all taken into custody during a raid in Sinaloa on Friday night, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said on X .

Elite military agents were able to find the targets and then arrive surreptitiously in the area, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said. The agents set perimeters around a residence to prevent Meza-Flores from escaping, while also defending the area from reinforcements who could have interrupted the operation.

The arresting agents were attacked with gunfire and explosives, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said. Seven attackers were killed during the operation. The agents entered the house and captured Meza-Flores, his two lieutenants, and five other suspected criminals. They also recovered drugs, cash, 10 firearms, a grenade launcher and other ammunition and weapons.

Meza-Flores and his lieutenants were flown to Mexico City and placed in custody of the Specialized Prosecutor's Office for Organized Crime. The other five arrestees were taken into custody in Sinaloa, the Mexican National Defense Secretariat said. One of those arrested is a first cousin of Meza-Flores and a logistics operator for the cartel.
Video shared by authorities shows heavily armed men in camouflage marching a man who appeared to be Meza-Flores through a dimly lit house and putting him in the back of a truck.

The Mexican government said in an early Saturday report that intelligence from the Trump administration helped authorities capture him, but provided few details about how the two countries coordinated. U.S. ambassador to Mexico Ronald Johnson said on X that "strategic intelligence sharing" between the U.S. and Mexico "helped make this operation possible."

In a social media post Saturday, U.S. Attorney General Todd Blanche said that Meza-Flores had ben captured "in an operation by the Mexican government supported by a coordinated interagency effort that included" the U.S. Homeland Security Task Force.

Videos and photos from the city of Guasave, Sinaloa, where Meza-Flores was captured, show screaming civilians fleeing gunfire at a baseball game, as well as burnt cars. The Mexican National Defense Secretariat said that four members of the Mexican Army's regular infantry forces "traveling to reinforce security" in the town have been killed.

Meza-Flores was indicted in 2012, then again in 2019. He faces multiple counts of drug-trafficking violations and the use and possession of a firearm. The FBI has described him as armed and dangerous. U.S. authorities had previously offered a reward of up to $5 million for information that led to Meza-Flores' arrest.

The high-profile capture comes as Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum faces pressure from President Trump to crack down on cartels. Sheinbaum has gone after illegal groups more aggressively than her predecessors, and homicides have dipped significantly in her two years in office.

The government has knocked out several cartel kingpins. Chief among them was Mexico's most powerful cartel leader , known as "El Mencho ," who was killed in February. Similar to the capture of Meza Flores, the dramatic operation resulted in a burst of violence and burning cars.
Mexican Security Secretary Omar García Harfuch wrote in a post on X Saturday morning that armed forces would remain deployed in the state of Sinaloa to protect civilians.
"These detentions are an important step in pacifying Sinaloa," he said.
The Associated Press contributed to this report.

body_zh: 墨西哥逮捕联邦调查局十大通缉毒枭，引发锡那罗亚州暴力 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
墨西哥军方周六宣布，已抓获联邦调查局十大通缉犯名单上的一名毒枭。随后锡那罗亚州爆发暴力事件，令平民不安。
福斯托·伊西德罗·梅萨-弗洛雷斯，也被称为“矮子伊西德罗”，据称是梅萨-弗洛雷斯跨国犯罪组织的领导人，联邦调查局将其描述为总部位于锡那罗亚州的“全副武装的主要贩毒组织”。
据联邦调查局称，该贩毒集团据称负责海洛因、甲基苯丙胺、可卡因、芬太尼和大麻的持有、分销和进口到美国，并控制了整个墨西哥的毒品生产、运输和分销。
墨西哥国防秘书处 10 日表示，梅萨-弗洛雷斯、他的副手“德国人”和卡特尔金融运营商“何塞·N”均在周五晚上锡那罗亚州的一次突袭中被拘留。
墨西哥国防秘书处表示，精锐军事特工能够找到目标，然后秘密抵达该地区。特工们在住宅周围设置了警戒线，以防止梅萨-弗洛雷斯逃跑，同时也保护该地区免受可能中断行动的增援部队的袭击。
墨西哥国防秘书处表示，逮捕人员遭到枪击和爆炸物袭击。七名袭击者在行动中被打死。特工进入房屋并抓获了梅萨-弗洛雷斯、他的两名副官以及其他五名犯罪嫌疑人。他们还缴获了毒品、现金、10支枪支、一个榴弹发射器以及其他弹药和武器。
梅萨-弗洛雷斯和他的副手被空运到墨西哥城，并被有组织犯罪特别检察官办公室拘留。墨西哥国防秘书处表示，其他五名被捕者已在锡那罗亚州被拘留。其中一名被捕者是梅萨-弗洛雷斯的表弟，也是该贩毒集团的一名物流操作员。
当局分享的视频显示，身着迷彩服的全副武装男子押着一名疑似梅萨-弗洛雷斯的男子穿过一间灯光昏暗的房子，并将他放到一辆卡车的后座上。
墨西哥政府在周六早些时候的一份报告中表示，特朗普政府的情报帮助当局抓获了他，但没有提供有关两国如何协调的细节。美国驻墨西哥大使罗纳德·约翰逊在 X 上表示，美国和墨西哥之间的“战略情报共享”“有助于使这次行动成为可能”。
美国司法部长托德·布兰奇在周六的社交媒体帖子中表示，梅萨-弗洛雷斯是在“墨西哥政府的一次行动中被抓获的，该行动得到了包括”美国国土安全特别工作组在内的跨部门协调努力的支持。
梅萨-弗洛雷斯被抓获的锡那罗亚州瓜萨维市的视频和照片显示，棒球比赛中平民尖叫着逃离枪击，汽车也被烧毁。墨西哥国防秘书处表示，墨西哥陆军正规步兵部队的四名成员在该镇“前往加强安全”时被杀。
梅萨-弗洛雷斯于 2012 年被起诉，随后于 2019 年再次被起诉。他面临多项贩毒违法以及使用和持有枪支罪名。联邦调查局称他武装且危险。美国当局此前曾悬赏高达 500 万美元，奖励提供导致梅萨-弗洛雷斯被捕的信息。
此次高调抓捕事件发生之际，墨西哥总统克劳迪娅·辛鲍姆面临特朗普总统要求打击卡特尔的压力。希因鲍姆比她的前任更积极地打击非法团体，在她执政的两年里，凶杀案大幅下降。
政府已经打掉了几名卡特尔头目。其中最主要的是墨西哥最有权势的贩毒集团头目，人称“El Mencho”，他于二月被杀。与占领梅萨弗洛雷斯类似，这次戏剧性的行动导致了一系列暴力事件和焚烧汽车。
墨西哥安全部长奥马尔·加西亚·哈富奇周六上午在一篇帖子中写道，武装部队将继续部署在锡那罗亚州以保护平民。
“这些拘留是平息锡那罗亚州的重要一步，”他说。
美联社对此报道作出了贡献。

title_en: Trump vows to work with Democrats to cap credit card interest rates at 10%
title_zh: 特朗普誓言与民主党合作将信用卡利率限制在10%
summary: President Trump says he will work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates
summary_zh: 特朗普总统表示，他将与即将上任的民主党国会合作限制信用卡利率
body_en: President Trump says he will work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates

NEW YORK -- President Donald Trump said Saturday that he would work with the incoming Democratic Congress to cap credit card interest rates , hoping to fulfill a promise he made on the 2024 campaign trail but couldn’t deliver on because of industry pressure and a lack of interest from his fellow Republicans.
“I would do it. These credit card companies have made a lot,” Trump told Fox News Channel's “Saturday in America.”

Democrats and the Republican president have both backed capping credit card interest rates, with the standard proposal being capping rates at 10%. It would substantially reduce what credit card companies can charge customers . The median credit card interest rate is roughly 22.2%, according to an August survey by the New York Federal Reserve.

Trump proposed capping credit card interest rates in January, as part of the White House’s affordability push . Banks and credit card companies immediately and aggressively opposed the proposal, saying any interest rate cap would force them to cancel cards for the poor and less creditworthy customers or substantially cut back on the rewards they offer when customers spend on their cards.
The proposal also did not sit well with Republicans, and there was little effort by the GOP-controlled Congress to fulfill Trump’s promise.

That could change now that Democrats will control both the House and Senate. Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., who is expected to be the next chair of the Senate Banking Committee, has said repeatedly she wants to cap rates.
In response to the Fox News interview, Warren said: “Let’s cap credit card interest rates and save Americans money.”

Other Democrats have endorsed the idea in various ways, including Rep. Maxine Waters of California, a powerful Democrat who sits on the House Financial Services Committee. Among Republicans, Sen. Josh Hawley of Missouri has proposed several caps on credit card interest rates, as recently as this year when Trump made his proposal.
“Congress should pass my bipartisan bill to cap these rates and deliver relief right away," Hawley said at the time.

Researchers who studied Trump’s campaign pledge after it was first announced found that Americans would save roughly $100 billion in interest a year if credit card rates were capped at 10%. The same researchers found that while the credit card industry would take a major hit, it would still be profitable, although credit card rewards and other perks might be scaled back.
About 195 million people in the United States had credit cards in 2024 and were assessed $160 billion in interest charges, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau says.
Americans are now carrying more credit card debt than ever, to the tune of about $1.23 trillion, according to figures from the New York Federal Reserve for the third quarter last year.
body_zh: 特朗普总统表示，他将与即将上任的民主党国会合作限制信用卡利率
纽约——唐纳德·特朗普总统周六表示，他将与即将上任的民主党国会合作限制信用卡利率，希望履行他在 2024 年竞选中做出的承诺，但由于行业压力和共和党同僚缺乏兴趣而未能兑现。
“我会这么做。这些信用卡公司赚了很多钱，”特朗普在福克斯新闻频道的“美国周六”节目中说道。
民主党和共和党总统都支持限制信用卡利率，标准提案是将利率限制在 10%。这将大大减少信用卡公司向客户收取的费用。根据纽约联储 8 月份的调查，信用卡利率中位数约为 22.2%。
特朗普在一月份提议限制信用卡利率，作为白宫推动负担能力的一部分。银行和信用卡公司立即强烈反对这一提议，称任何利率上限都将迫使他们取消为贫困和信用较差的客户提供的信用卡，或者大幅削减客户在信用卡上消费时提供的奖励。
该提案也不受共和党人的欢迎，共和党控制的国会几乎没有做出任何努力来履行特朗普的承诺。
现在民主党将控制众议院和参议院，这种情况可能会改变。预计将成为参议院银行委员会下一任主席的马萨诸塞州民主党参议员伊丽莎白·沃伦 (Elizabeth Warren) 曾多次表示，她希望限制利率。
沃伦在回应福克斯新闻采访时表示：“让我们限制信用卡利率，为美国人省钱。”

其他民主党人以各种方式支持这一想法，其中包括众议院金融服务委员会成员、加州众议员玛克辛·沃特斯 (Maxine Waters)，她是一位实力强大的民主党人。在共和党人中，密苏里州参议员乔什·霍利 (Josh Hawley) 曾提议对信用卡利率设定几项上限，就在今年特朗普提出这一提议时。
霍利当时表示：“国会应该通过我的两党法案来限制这些利率并立即提供救济。”
研究人员在特朗普的竞选承诺首次宣布后对其进行了研究，结果发现，如果信用卡利率上限为 10%，美国人每年将节省约 1000 亿美元的利息。同一批研究人员发现，虽然信用卡行业将遭受重大打击，但它仍然有利可图，尽管信用卡奖励和其他福利可能会减少。
消费者金融保护局表示，到 2024 年，美国约有 1.95 亿人拥有信用卡，并被收取了 1,600 亿美元的利息费用。
根据纽约联储去年第三季度的数据，美国人现在背负的信用卡债务比以往任何时候都多，达到约 1.23 万亿美元。

title_en: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow
title_zh: 路易斯安那州男子被控在徒步小径上杀害妇女并用十字弓谋杀同事
summary: Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a cross
summary_zh: 贾里德·舒尔 (Jared Schurr) 在利泽特·罗德里格斯 (Lizeht Rodriguez) 和伍德罗·斯科特 (Woodrow Scott) 死于其他无关的杀戮后在密西西比州被捕。
body_en: Louisiana man charged with killing woman on hiking trail and murdering co-worker with crossbow | Louisiana
Jared Schurr arrested in Mississippi after Lizeht Rodriguez and Woodrow Scott died in otherwise unrelated killings

A man recently strangled a woman to death whom he did not know along a hiking trail north of New Orleans – then killed his co-worker with a crossbow two days later before being arrested in Mississippi after a police chase, authorities allege.
Jared Schurr, 36, faces counts of second-degree murder in the killings of Lizeht Rodriguez, 24, and Woodrow Scott, 37, on 11 and 13 November, respectively, investigators said on Saturday.
As described by officials, Rodriguez’s death is a chilling example of a case not often seen in the US: a random murder by a stranger.

Rodriguez body was found slain at the Northlake nature center in Mandeville, Louisiana . On Saturday, detectives with the local St Tammany parish sheriff’s office major crimes unit obtained an arrest warrant accusing Schurr of second-degree murder in connection with Rodriguez’s death, the agency said in a statement.
The statement said: “Schurr confessed to encountering Rodriguez, whom he did not know, while walking along a trail at the Northlake nature center.

“Schurr told detectives he passed Rodriguez on the trail before grabbing and strangling her, then dragging her body to the area where she was later discovered by another person walking along the trail,” the statement continued.

At the time that St Tammany investigators obtained that warrant, Schurr was already wanted by the sheriff’s office in connection with a separate homicide that occurred two days after Rodriguez’s killing.

Schurr in that case is suspected of shooting his co-worker Scott in the back with a crossbow. He was arrested on 13 November after a vehicle chase that began near Bogalusa, Louisiana – north of Mandeville – and ended in Pearl River county, Mississippi .
As of Saturday, Schurr was being held in custody in the Pearl River jail pending extradition to Louisiana.
Authorities said they homed in on Schurr after an investigation involving assistance from the FBI and license-plate reading cameras.

The St Tammany parish sheriff’s office said its detectives were awaiting the results of DNA analysis which were expected to provide additional evidence linking Schurr to Rodriguez’s murder. The agency also said it would continue looking into both homicides to determine what the motive may have been.

FBI research estimates that fewer than 10% of murder victims are killed by people not known to them. The vast majority of people murdered are instead victimized by people they know, according to that research.
body_zh: 路易斯安那州男子被控在徒步小径上杀害妇女并用十字弓谋杀同事路易斯安那州
利泽特·罗德里格斯和伍德罗·斯科特死于其他无关的杀戮后，贾里德·舒尔在密西西比州被捕
当局称，一名男子最近在新奥尔良北部的一条远足小道上勒死了一名他不认识的女子，两天后又用十字弓杀死了他的同事，最后在警方追捕后在密西西比州被捕。
调查人员周六表示，36 岁的贾里德·舒尔 (Jared Schurr) 因分别于 11 月 11 日和 11 月 13 日杀害 24 岁的利泽特·罗德里格斯 (Lizeht Rodriguez) 和 37 岁的伍德罗·斯科特 (Woodrow Scott) 而面临二级谋杀罪。
据官员描述，罗德里格斯之死是美国不常见案件的一个令人毛骨悚然的例子：陌生人随机谋杀。
罗德里格斯的尸体在路易斯安那州曼德维尔的诺斯莱克自然中心被发现被杀。该机构在一份声明中表示，周六，当地圣坦慕尼教区警长办公室重大犯罪部门的侦探获得了逮捕令，指控舒尔犯有与罗德里格斯之死有关的二级谋杀罪。
声明称：“舒尔承认，他在北湖自然中心的一条小路上行走时遇到了他不认识的罗德里格斯。
声明继续说道：“舒尔告诉侦探，他在小路上经过了罗德里格斯，然后抓住并勒死了她，然后将她的尸体拖到了她后来被沿着小路行走的另一个人发现的地方。”
当圣坦慕尼调查人员获得逮捕令时，舒尔已经被治安官办公室通缉，原因是他与罗德里格斯被杀两天后发生的另一起凶杀案有关。
在该案中，舒尔涉嫌用十字弓射中他的同事斯科特的背部。 11 月 13 日，他在路易斯安那州博加卢萨附近（曼德维尔以北）开始并在密西西比州珠河县结束的一场汽车追逐中被捕。
截至周六，舒尔被关押在珠江监狱，等待引渡到路易斯安那州。
当局表示，在联邦调查局和车牌读取摄像头的协助下进行调查后，他们对舒尔进行了调查。
圣坦慕尼教区警长办公室表示，侦探们正在等待 DNA 分析结果，预计该结果将提供更多证据，将舒尔与罗德里格斯谋杀案联系起来。该机构还表示，将继续调查这两起凶杀案，以确定其动机是什么。
FBI 研究估计，只有不到 10% 的谋杀案受害者是被不认识的人杀害的。根据这项研究，绝大多数被谋杀的人都是他们认识的人的受害者。

title_en: Trump says reported FBI database hack is ‘not good’
title_zh: 特朗普称联邦调查局数据库遭黑客攻击的报道“不好”
summary: The FBI is reportedly investigating a hack of the National Crime Information Center.
summary_zh: 据报道，联邦调查局正在调查国家犯罪信息中心的黑客攻击事件。
body_en: Trump says reported FBI database hack is ‘not good’ | TechCrunch
The FBI is investigating an apparent hack of the National Crime Information Center (NCIC), according to reports in CNN and the Associated Press .
The NCIC is the online database used by federal and local law enforcement to share information about warrants, background checks, and more. The scope of the breach does not yet appear to be clear.

A former FBI official told CNN that they’re not just concerned about “whether hackers gained access to sensitive information, although that is an issue, but whether they could compromise the accuracy of the information that officers rely on.”

President Donald Trump addressed the reports during an interview Saturday with Fox News, saying, “We just heard about it and I will say that it’s not good.” At the same time, Trump also said that as a result of the breach, “maybe we’ll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise because, you know, you had the Russia, Russia, Russia hoax.”
In September, the FBI reportedly told agents and support staff that their personal information had been stolen in a cyberattack .
