title_en: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial
title_zh: 共和党参议员因 1 月 6 日否认而阻止特朗普网络提名人
summary: Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’ Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vo
summary_zh: 汤姆·蒂利斯 (Thom Tillis) 的举动是在获得 CISA 职位提名的迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 在听证会上表示：“我不相信这是一次袭击”。
body_en: Republican senator blocks Trump cyber nominee over January 6 denial | Republicans
Thom Tillis move comes after Michael LoSapio, nominated for Cisa role, told hearing ‘I don’t believe it was an attack’

Senator Thom Tillis, the outgoing North Carolina Republican who is due to be replaced by a Democrat, has reportedly blocked a confirmation vote on Donald Trump’s nominee to lead a key US cybersecurity agency, Michael LoSapio, after he denied during a hearing that the Capitol was attacked on January 6 2021.

Tillis, who declined to run for re-election and after repeated clashes with Trump’s, confirmed to HuffPost on Friday that he has placed a hold on LoSapio’s nomination to serve as a director of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Agency (Cisa). His block on the nomination will prevent it from being included in a package of nominees to be voted on next month, before the Republicans lose their majority in the Senate.

At his Senate confirmation hearing on Thursday, LoSapio, the chief information security officer for Palantir, a technology firm founded by JD Vance’s mentor, Peter Thiel, was asked by senator Richard Blumenthal, a Connecticut Democrat: “Was there an attack on the Capitol of January 6 2021?”
After initially replying, “I don’t know,” LoSapio said: “No, I don’t believe it was an attack.”
Tillis told the Hill that the question of whether a mob of Trump supporters attacked the US Capitol in an attempt to overturn Joe Biden’s 2020 victory was not open for debate.
“It’s binary,” Tillis told the outlet. “The minute you pretend like it didn’t exist or you can’t even acknowledge it, I don’t have any time because it’s not a very thoughtful person.”
The agency LoSapio was nominated by Trump to lead, Cisa, plays a role in protecting US elections infrastructure from hacking.

The week after the 2020 election, as Trump falsely claimed that count had been rigged, Cisa was one of a number of federal agencies with oversight of election infrastructure to issue a statement calling the election “the most secure in American history” and noting that there was “no evidence that any voting system deleted or lost votes, changed votes, or was in any way compromised.”

After he returned to the White House last year, Trump signed an April 2025 presidential memorandum directing executive offices to take steps to address supposed “risks from Chris Krebs”, who led Cisa in 2020.

“Krebs, through CISA, falsely and baselessly denied that the 2020 election was rigged and stolen, including by inappropriately and categorically dismissing widespread election malfeasance and serious vulnerabilities with voting machines,” Trump’s memorandum claimed.
body_zh: 共和党参议员因 1 月 6 日否认而阻止特朗普网络提名人 |共和党人
Thom Tillis 的举动是在 Cisa 角色提名的 Michael LoSapio 在听证会上表示“我不相信这是一次袭击”之后发生的。
据报道，即将卸任的北卡罗来纳州共和党参议员汤姆·蒂利斯 (Thom Tillis) 将由民主党人接替。据报道，他在听证会上否认国会大厦于 2021 年 1 月 6 日遭到袭击后，阻止了对唐纳德·特朗普 (Donald Trump) 领导美国重要网络安全机构的提名人迈克尔·洛萨皮奥 (Michael LoSapio) 的确认投票。
蒂利斯在与特朗普多次发生冲突后拒绝竞选连任，周五向《赫芬顿邮报》证实，他已暂停洛萨皮奥担任美国网络安全和基础设施局（Cisa）局长的提名。在共和党失去参议院多数席位之前，他对提名的阻止将导致该提名无法被纳入下个月投票表决的一揽子提名人中。
在周四的参议院确认听证会上，JD Vance 的导师 Peter Thiel 创立的科技公司 Palantir 的首席信息安全官 LoSapio 被康涅狄格州民主党参议员理查德·布卢门撒尔问到：“2021 年 1 月 6 日国会大厦是否发生过袭击？”
洛萨皮奥最初回答“我不知道”后说道：“不，我不相信这是一次攻击。”
蒂利斯告诉国会山，特朗普支持者的暴徒袭击美国国会大厦是否是为了推翻乔·拜登 2020 年的胜利，这个问题没有争议。
“这是二元的，”蒂利斯告诉媒体。 “一旦你假装它不存在，或者你甚至无法承认它，我就没有时间了，因为它不是一个很有思想的人。”
由特朗普提名领导的机构 LoSapio Cisa 在保护美国选举基础设施免遭黑客攻击方面发挥着作用。
2020 年大选结束后一周，特朗普错误地声称计票被操纵，CISA 是众多负责监督选举基础设施的联邦机构之一，他们发表声明称这次选举是“美国历史上最安全的一次”，并指出“没有证据表明任何投票系统删除或丢失选票、更改选票或以任何方式受到损害”。
去年重返白宫后，特朗普于 2025 年 4 月签署了一份总统备忘录，指示行政办公室采取措施应对所谓的“来自 2020 年领导 CISA 的克里斯·克雷布斯 (Chris Krebs) 的风险”。
特朗普的备忘录称，“克雷布斯通过 CISA 虚假且毫无根据地否认 2020 年选举被操纵和盗窃，包括不恰当地断然否认普遍存在的选举舞弊行为和投票机的严重漏洞。”

title_en: Trump auditions potential successors as Rubio and Vance join him for White House briefing
title_zh: 卢比奥和万斯与特朗普一起参加白宫简报会，特朗普试镜潜在的继任者
summary: It was the latest episode in the public audition that the president and former reality television star has appeared to delight in arranging for his potential successors as he nears his last two years in office.
summary_zh: 这是公开试镜的最新一集，总统和前电视真人秀明星似乎很高兴为他的节目安排。
body_en: Jonathan J. Cooper, Associated Press Jonathan J. Cooper, Associated Press
https://www.pbs.org/newshour/politics/trump-auditions-potential-successors-as-rubio-and-vance-join-him-for-white-house-briefing
Marco Rubio fidgeted and sighed. JD Vance smiled and furrowed his brow.

For 90 minutes on Friday, the secretary of state and the vice president, both potential 2028 presidential contenders, stood nearly shoulder to shoulder in matching outfits, an arm's length from President Donald Trump as he spoke to reporters crowded into the White House press briefing room.
WATCH: What Trump addressed during his lengthy White House news conference

It was the latest episode in the public audition that the president and former reality television star has appeared to delight in arranging for his potential successors as he nears his last two years in office.

In the same room months earlier, Rubio and Vance each took a turn defending the president and selling his agenda while filling in as White House press secretary. The president has also been known to quiz his public and private audiences on their opinions of the two men.
Vance and Rubio maintain that they're good friends and have both demurred about whether they'll seek the White House in the next presidential race. Rubio has said he won't run if Vance does.
Even so, the race to succeed Trump as the GOP nominee is quietly heating up, with Vance and Rubio widely seen as some of the likeliest contenders.
One by one, Trump called them to the lectern, turning his gaze from them to the audience as he surveyed how each of their remarks landed with the dozens of journalists in the room.
He explained that it was in his job description to stay in Washington while Trump, Rubio and others were on the other side of the world for international summits in the Philippines and China.
Vance said he had to "stay back and hold down the fort," like the movie "Home Alone," but "with better food and more gold" at the White House.
"So, I missed you, sir," Vance said before shifting into lauding Trump's economic leadership.

Trump said Vance's statement distancing himself from the war in Iran and blaming it for the GOP's midterm losses was "fine" and "accurate." Notably, Vance passed on an opportunity to say the Iran war was worth the political costs.
WATCH: Trump hosts news conference after meeting with Xi, Putin
"I think the president is the one who makes the decision, and the president has said he would do it again," Vance said.
As Trump spoke, Vance laughed at his jokes but stood mostly still, hands clasped in front of himself with a serious expression on his face.
Rubio, by contrast, fidgeted behind Trump, turning from side to side and adjusting his tie. At one point, he pulled a note out of his breast pocket to review it.

When Rubio took the microphone, he spoke in his typical rapid-fire clip as he recapped Trump's Asia trip and forcefully defended Trump's decision to meet the authoritarian leaders of China and Russia.
body_zh: 乔纳森·J·库珀，美联社 乔纳森·J·库珀，美联社
马可·卢比奥坐立不安，叹了口气。 JD万斯微笑着皱起眉头。
周五的 90 分钟里，国务卿和副总统这两位 2028 年总统候选人的潜在竞争者几乎并肩站立，穿着相配的服装，与唐纳德·特朗普总统在白宫新闻发布室对挤满的记者发表讲话时保持一臂距离。
观看：特朗普在漫长的白宫新闻发布会上发表的讲话
这是公开试镜的最新一集，这位总统和前真人秀明星似乎很高兴在他任期的最后两年之际安排他的潜在继任者。
几个月前，在同一个房间里，卢比奥和万斯轮流为总统辩护并推销他的议程，同时担任白宫新闻秘书。众所周知，总统还向公众和私人听众询问他们对这两个人的看法。
万斯和卢比奥坚称他们是好朋友，并且都对是否会在下届总统竞选中入主白宫提出异议。卢比奥表示，如果万斯参选，他也不会参选。
即便如此，接替特朗普成为共和党提名人的竞争正在悄然升温，万斯和卢比奥被广泛视为最有可能的竞争者。
特朗普一一把他们叫到讲台上，把目光从他们身上转向观众，审视他们的每一条言论如何受到房间里数十名记者的欢​​迎。
他解释说，他的工作职责是留在华盛顿，而特朗普、卢比奥和其他人则在世界的另一边参加在菲律宾和中国举行的国际峰会。
万斯表示，他必须像电影《小鬼当家》一样，“留在后方守住堡垒”，但要在白宫“提供更好的食物和更多的黄金”。
“所以，我想念你，先生，”万斯说道，然后转而赞扬特朗普的经济领导力。
特朗普表示，万斯将自己与伊朗战争保持距离并将共和党中期失败归咎于伊朗战争的声明“很好”且“准确”。值得注意的是，万斯错过了一个表示伊朗战争值得付出政治代价的机会。
观看：特朗普在与习近平和普京会面后主持新闻发布会
万斯说：“我认为总统是做出决定的人，总统已经说过他会再次这样做。”
特朗普讲话时，万斯听了他的笑话，大笑起来，但他几乎一动不动地站着，双手紧握在身前，脸上表情严肃。
相比之下，卢比奥在特朗普身后坐立不安，左右转过身，调整着领带。有一次，他从胸前的口袋里掏出一张纸条来查看。
当卢比奥拿起麦克风时，他以典型的连珠炮式讲话，回顾了特朗普的亚洲之行，并为特朗普会见中国和俄罗斯独裁领导人的决定进行了有力的辩护。

title_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad
title_zh: 特朗普威胁对在海外建立数据中心的美国科技公司实施“巨额处罚”
summary: President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he
summary_zh: 总统在白宫举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会，并表示他与普京和习近平有着“极好的关系”唐纳德·特朗普威胁弗里达
body_en: Trump threatens ‘tremendous penalties’ for US tech firms that build datacenters abroad | Donald Trump
President gives wide-ranging White House press conference and says he has ‘fantastic relationships’ with Putin and Xi

Donald Trump threatened on Friday to impose “tremendous penalties” on American tech companies that build datacenters outside the US, though he gave no details and told reporters he had not yet informed his own officials about the plan.

In a discursive press conference from the White House briefing room, Trump also said he would “look into” the report that Iran had been planning to possibly detonate a “dirty bomb” in Washington DC, and backed JD Vance over comments the vice-president made blaming Republican midterm losses on the Iran war.

Trump also expounded on his friendship with the Russian president Vladimir Putin, whom he met alongside China’s Xi Jinping at the Apec summit on Thursday, adding he had “fantastic relationships” with both autocratic leaders.
At the White House, Trump told reporters he wanted datacenters built by US companies to stay on US soil.

“We’re not allowing datacenters to go into other countries, because China will take all of them, and we’re not allowing that to happen. And we’re going to put tremendous penalties on companies that try to do it,” he said.
He said Americans should welcome datacenters, and urged communities to extract concessions from developers, repeating a point he made before the midterms.
“You ought to take advantage of the datacenters. Make them pay you, make them pay your community, but don’t shut them off,” he said.

With many Americans turning against the datacenters being built near their homes, the US tech industry is making a show of conciliation by promising to take fewer government handouts, to be more transparent, and to give more money to towns and cities willing to allow server warehouses to be built.

The Trump administration on Monday issued new rules to restrict remote access to advanced US computing chips and servers, in a move it said was designed to limit China’s ability to use US chips to train its artificial intelligence models – though a House committee said on Wednesday the US had signed off on sales of nearly 900,000 AI chips to China in six months.

China’s ability to obtain advanced AI chips made by the US firm Nvidia, in which Trump is an investor, has been spotlighted in recent weeks after its CEO, Jensen Huang, was fired over his affair with a woman alleged to be spying for China.

In the same press conference, Trump was asked about reports Iran was planning to potentially detonate an explosive laced with nuclear material – a so-called “dirty bomb” – in Washington DC. The president called it a “rumour” and said: “If they do, we’re going to fight.”
He added: “We know a lot about what’s happening in Iran. We know everything they say. We know who they are, where they are. We’ll find out about it.”
Responding to a question about reports of a rift with Vance, Trump said the vice-president’s remark blaming the Republican collapse on the Iran war was “a very accurate statement”.

“I didn’t say I was unhappy with it,” the president said. “I would have added one other thing if it were asked … would you do it again? And absolutely, the answer is yes, because we cannot allow Iran to have a nuclear weapon.”
Trump was asked whether Vladimir Putin could really be considered a friend to America since Russia is a close ally of Iran.

“I can’t speak to America,” he said, adding: “I consider [that] I have fantastic relationships with Putin. That’s a very good thing. I have fantastic relationships with President Xi. That’s a good thing, and our country is safe because of that.”
He praised Putin as he repeated his grievances over the Department of Justice’s investigation into the Russian attempts to influence US voters ahead of the 2016 presidential election.
body_zh: 特朗普威胁对在海外建设数据中心的美国科技公司实施“巨额处罚”唐纳德·特朗普
总统在白宫举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会，并表示他与普京和习近平有着“极好的关系”
唐纳德·特朗普周五威胁要对在美国境外建立数据中心的美国科技公司实施“巨额处罚”，但他没有透露细节，并告诉记者，他尚未将该计划告知本国官员。
在白宫新闻发布会上，特朗普还表示，他将“调查”伊朗计划在华盛顿特区引爆“脏弹”的报道，并支持副总统万斯将共和党中期选举失败归咎于伊朗战争的言论。
特朗普还阐述了他与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京的友谊，他在周四的亚太经合组织峰会上与中国国家主席习近平会面，并补充说他与两位独裁领导人有着“极好的关系”。
特朗普在白宫告诉记者，他希望美国公司建造的数据中心留在美国领土上。
“我们不允许数据中心进入其他国家，因为中国将把它们全部拿走，我们不会允许这种情况发生。我们将对试图这样做的公司处以巨额处罚，”他说。
他表示美国人应该欢迎数据中心，并敦促社区从开发商那里获得让步，重复了他在中期选举前提出的观点。
“你应该利用数据中心。让他们付钱给你，让他们付钱给你的社区，但不要关闭它们，”他说。
随着许多美国人反对在他们家附近建造数据中心，美国科技行业正在做出和解的姿态，承诺减少政府的施舍，提高透明度，并向愿意允许建造服务器仓库的城镇提供更多资金。
特朗普政府周一发布了新规则，限制远程访问美国先进计算芯片和服务器，据称此举旨在限制中国使用美国芯片训练其人工智能模型的能力，尽管众议院委员会周三表示，美国已批准在六个月内向中国出售近 90 万个人工智能芯片。
最近几周，在特朗普投资的美国公司英伟达 (Nvidia) 首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 因与一名涉嫌为中国从事间谍活动的女性有染而被解雇后，中国获得特朗普投资的英伟达 (Nvidia) 制造的先进人工智能芯片的能力受到关注。
在同一次新闻发布会上，特朗普被问及有关伊朗计划在华盛顿特区引爆含有核材料的爆炸物（所谓的“脏弹”）的报道。总统称其为“谣言”，并表示：“如果他们这样做，我们就会战斗。”
他补充道：“我们对伊朗正在发生的事情了解很多。我们知道他们所说的一切。我们知道他们是谁，他们在哪里。我们会查明真相的。”
在回答有关与万斯不和的报道的问题时，特朗普表示，副总统将共和党崩溃归咎于伊朗战争的言论是“非常准确的声明”。
“我没有说我对此不满意，”总统说。 “如果有人问我，我会补充一件事……你会再这样做吗？绝对，答案是肯定的，因为我们不能允许伊朗拥有核武器。”
特朗普被问及弗拉基米尔·普京是否真的可以被视为美国的朋友，因为俄罗斯是伊朗的亲密盟友。
“我无法与美国交谈，”他补充道，“我认为我与普京的关系非常好。这是一件非常好的事情。我与习主席的关系非常好。这是一件好事，因此我们的国家是安全的。”
他赞扬了普京，并重申了他对司法部对俄罗斯试图在 2016 年总统选举前影响美国选民的调查的不满。

title_en: Families frustrated with Pentagon probe of deadly drone strike
title_zh: 五角大楼对致命无人机袭击事件的调查让许多家庭感到沮丧
summary: The Pentagon is preparing to release findings of its investigation into the attack that killed six U.S. soldiers in Kuwait early in the Iran war.
summary_zh: 五角大楼正准备公布对伊朗战争初期在科威特造成六名美国士兵死亡的袭击事件的调查结果。
body_en: Gold Star families frustrated with Pentagon investigation into Iran drone strike that killed 6 soldiers - CBS News

Gold Star families have told CBS News that briefings about a forthcoming U.S. military report on the deadliest strike on U.S. soldiers in the Iran conflict did not, to their satisfaction, address their concerns about the military preparations and response to the attack.

Several of the families said they have been briefed about the unclassified results from the long-awaited internal probe into one of the first attacks on U.S. troops during Operation Epic Fury. Six U.S. Army Reserve soldiers were killed by a drone strike on their command post in Kuwait, known as Port Shuaiba, on March 1.
The official report has not yet been released to the public. The Pentagon has indicated it could be made public in a matter of days.
Over the past week, the Army briefed at least three Gold Star families on the investigation, and several family members told CBS News they were frustrated by what they heard.

Some of those briefed told CBS News the report does little to address the findings of an eight-month CBS News investigation, in which multiple sources said Army commanders ignored repeated warnings about the drone threat in the weeks before the attack.

Witnesses told CBS News that the facilities were not fortified to protect service members from a strike by one-way attack drones, which are a staple of the Iranian arsenal. Soldiers on the site said they had seen U.S. intelligence prior to the war showing the location was on an Iranian target list. And they argued the facilities lacked sufficient medical supplies and a plan for a mass casualty incident.

The briefings were led by Brig. Gen. Peter Glass, the deputy commander of U.S. Army Central, according to those who attended. They were individually held at either military or National Guard posts in locations close to the respective families.

"I wish I felt better," a Gold Star family member told CBS News after her briefing, which she said lasted roughly three hours. "I wish this gave me more than what I had yesterday or what I had the day before."

The briefings come just days after a U.S. Army soldier who survived the deadly Iranian drone attack filed a whistleblower complaint to Congress alleging senior military officials ignored warnings and did not plan properly for anti-drone defenses ahead of the war with Iran.

The whistleblower, Army Maj. Stephen Ramsbottom, spoke exclusively with 60 Minutes' Norah O'Donnell about his complaint, which was submitted to the House and Senate Armed Services Committees on Nov. 13 and obtained by CBS News.

In the complaint, Ramsbottom alleges that Army leaders were warned about drone threats at the U.S. command post, and alleges the site had "no dedicated protection" against the Iranian drones. In an interview with CBS News, he identified Brig. Gen. Clint Barnes, who commanded the unit, and Maj. Gen. John Hinson, who oversaw logistics for the U.S. command, as dismissing warnings about protection at the location. Ramsbottom called for an independent investigation.
Neither official responded to multiple requests for comment from CBS News.

Another Gold Star family member described the briefing as mostly "cordial" but said the exchange grew tense when family members pressed for more answers about why the unit was moved to Port Shuaiba when most other soldiers were sent out of Kuwait ahead of the launch of Operation Epic Fury.
"We took a couple breaks because it got heavy and I needed some air," one family member said.

Joey Amor, whose wife, Master Sgt. Nicole Amor, was among those killed, told 60 Minutes he believes she might have survived if there was a better plan in place. "I think my wife had a shot, yeah," he said.
He said investigators told him that, no matter what medical resources were present, his wife's injuries were too severe for her to have survived the strike.

The Pentagon for months has declined comment to CBS News, but confirmed its internal investigation into the Port Shuaiba attack concluded in June. Still, it would take until mid-November for the Army to share its findings — another point of contention for some Gold Star family members.
"Going in I had an idea of what I wanted to know," another family member said. "I just knew I wasn't going to get answers — and I was right."
This story published first on CBS News at 12:02 p.m. on Nov. 21, 2026.
body_zh: 金星家庭对五角大楼对伊朗无人机袭击造成 6 名士兵死亡的调查感到沮丧 - 哥伦比亚广播公司新闻
金星家属告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，关于即将发布的美国军事报告的简报，该报告涉及伊朗冲突中对美国士兵最致命的袭击，但令他们满意的是，他们并没有解决他们对军事准备和对袭击的反应的担忧。
一些家庭表示，他们已获悉对“史诗愤怒”行动中美军首次袭击事件进行期待已久的内部调查的非机密结果。 3 月 1 日，6 名美国陆军预备役士兵在科威特舒艾巴港指挥所遭到无人机袭击身亡。
官方报告尚未向公众发布。五角大楼表示，该信息可能会在几天内公开。
过去一周，陆军向至少三个金星家庭通报了调查情况，一些家庭成员告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，他们对所听到的情况感到沮丧。
一些知情人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，该报告几乎没有提及哥伦比亚广播公司新闻长达八个月的调查结果，多名消息人士称，陆军指挥官在袭击发生前几周无视了有关无人机威胁的反复警告。
目击者告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，这些设施没有加固，无法保护军人免受单向攻击无人机的袭击，而单向攻击无人机是伊朗武器库的主要武器。该网站上的士兵表示，他们在战前看到美国情报显示该地点位于伊朗目标名单上。他们认为这些设施缺乏足够的医疗用品和应对大规模伤亡事件的计划。
简报会由准将主持。据与会者称，美国中央陆军副司令彼得·格拉斯将军。他们被单独关押在靠近各自家庭的军事哨所或国民警卫队哨所。
“我希望我感觉好点，”一位金星家族成员在简报结束后告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，她说简报持续了大约三个小时。 “我希望这给了我比昨天或前天更多的东西。”
就在几天前，一名在致命的伊朗无人机袭击中幸存的美国陆军士兵向国会提出举报，指控高级军事官员无视警告，并且在与伊朗的战争之前没有适当规划反无人机防御。
举报人陆军少校斯蒂芬·拉姆斯博顿 (Stephen Ramsbottom) 接受了《60 分钟》节目的诺拉·奥唐纳 (Norah O'Donnell) 的独家采访，谈论了他的投诉。该投诉已于 11 月 13 日提交给众议院和参议院军事委员会，哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News) 获得了该投诉。
拉姆斯巴顿在诉状中声称，陆军领导人在美国指挥所收到了有关无人机威胁的警告，并声称该地点“没有针对伊朗无人机的专门保护措施”。在接受哥伦比亚广播公司新闻采访时，他确认了准将。该部队指挥官克林特·巴恩斯将军和负责美军司令部后勤工作的约翰·辛森少将对有关该地点保护的警告不以为然。拉姆斯博顿呼吁进行独立调查。
两位官员均未回应哥伦比亚广播公司新闻的多次置评请求。
另一名金星家族成员称这次简报大部分是“亲切的”，但他表示，当家族成员要求提供更多答案，解释为什么该部队被转移到舒艾巴港，而大多数其他士兵在“史诗愤怒”行动启动之前被派出科威特时，双方的交流变得紧张。
“我们休息了几次，因为天气很重，我需要一些空气，”一位家庭成员说。
乔伊·阿莫尔，他的妻子，军士长。遇难者之一的妮可·阿莫尔 (Nicole Amor) 告诉《60 分钟》节目，他相信如果有更好的计划，她可能会活下来。 “我想我的妻子有机会，是的，”他说。
他说，调查人员告诉他，无论有多少医疗资源，他妻子的伤势都太严重，无法在罢工中幸存。
五角大楼几个月来一直拒绝对哥伦比亚广播公司新闻发表评论，但证实其对舒艾巴港袭击事件的内部调查已于六月结束。尽管如此，陆军要到 11 月中旬才能分享其调查结果——这也是一些金星家族成员争论的另一个焦点。
另一位家庭成员说：“进去后我就知道了我想知道的事情。” “我只知道我不会得到答案——但我是对的。”
本文首先于哥伦比亚广播公司新闻 (CBS News) 中午 12 点 02 分发表。 2026 年 11 月 21 日。

title_en: The latest from Trump's press conference
title_zh: 特朗普新闻发布会的最新消息
summary: President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.
summary_zh: 特朗普总统在其历史性亚洲之行会见中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统后举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会
body_en: The latest from Trump's press conference President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.
President Trump gave a wide-ranging press conference following his historic trip to Asia where he met with Chinese President Xi and Russian President Putin.

President Trump returned to Washington after his three-day trip to Asia and took questions from the White House today. The trip included the first ever three-way meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin. But there was little in the way of agreements on key global issues.
PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP: The United States entered this trip from a position of unmatched economic and diplomatic strength.

CHANG: Well, all of this raises questions about the staying power of Trump's America-first approach and America's future role in the world. Joining us now is NPR White House correspondent Franco Ordoñez, who is in the room, and we have NPR national security correspondent Greg Myre. Hello to both of you.
CHANG: All right. So, Franco, did the president make any news in this press conference?

ORDOÑEZ: Yeah, I mean, not really. I mean, it was really a very meandering talk, starting off with highlights of his first two years in office. And then he probably spent about 30 minutes talking about his time abroad and, you know, recounting his relationship with Xi and Putin. He did say, though, that he and Xi had made some agreements about putting in guardrails - that's the word he used - with artificial intelligence, which he calls super intelligence. Here he is there.

TRUMP: It's not artificial intelligence. It's not artificial. It's super. Problem is, it may be too super. So President Xi and I agree that we're going to do some joint guardrails, the two of us, 'cause there really is no third place.

ORDOÑEZ: Now, of course, details are scarce, but the idea of guardrails is notable because Trump has pretty - previously, at least, been pretty allergic to any restrictions on developing AI. I mean, he has repeatedly said he's wanted to maintain a U.S. advantage over China.
CHANG: Right. OK, well, Greg, Trump had some things to say about chip sales to China and the whole Nvidia fallout, right? What struck you about his answers there?

MYRE: Yeah, I mean, Trump says he wants the U.S. to keep the lead in AI, as Franco just noted. And he also said he won't allow U.S. companies to build AI data centers outside the U.S. However, Trump is the one allowing Nvidia to sell advanced chips to China. Nvidia's Jensen Huang lobbied Trump last year and persuaded the president to allow these sales. And just yesterday, the House Foreign Affairs Committee released a list of requests this year by Nvidia and another chipmaker, AMD, to sell chips to Chinese company - companies. As of May this year, the Trump administration approved the sale of nearly 900,000 advanced chips, and they include big names like Alibaba and Tencent. And those two companies are also on a Pentagon list of Chinese firms that are linked to the Chinese military. So what does Trump actually want here? Does he want Nvidia to keep selling those chips to China, or does he want to block those sales?
CHANG: Good questions. Well, Trump was also asked about the whole change in leadership over cybersecurity, right? What did we learn there?

MYRE: Yeah, Trump fired the White House Cybersecurity Director Sean Carncross, and at the press conference today, he said, I don't think that person was good enough. Now, he's being replaced by Kirsten Davies, who's been the chief information officer at the Defense Department. And this is certainly an important position, but it's a policy position, not a hands on operational position.

The agency that's really important here is CISA, the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, which deals with election security and protecting government networks from cyberattacks. And this agency has not had a director since Trump became president almost two years ago. Now, as it happens, Trump's nomination to lead the agency, Michael LoSapio, had a Senate confirmation hearing yesterday. He was grilled by Democratic senators. He was asked who won the 2020 presidential election. He refused to answer. He was asked if the Capitol was attacked on January 6, 2021, and he said he didn't think it was an attack. So it's not clear that he'll be confirmed, but whoever winds up in this position will be in charge of election security in 2028.

CHANG: Interesting. OK, Franco, back to this meeting with Xi and Putin, which was designed to demonstrate American power, right? Do you think it also may have opened the door for allies to turn away from the U.S.?

ORDOÑEZ: Yeah, I mean, very much designed to demonstrate American power, but I also think it does show that power and influence are not the same thing. I mean, Trump was asked today if Putin, who he called his friend, was also America's friend.

ORDOÑEZ: You know, he really couldn't answer that. But he did continue to make the case that his relationship with Putin would reap benefits for America, though we haven't really seen that yet. You know, the war in Ukraine continues to rage on. But we are seeing allies start to build alliances with other nations as, you know, confidence in the U.S. falters, and they look to reduce their dependence on the U.S.
CHANG: Well, great. What about progress when it comes to Iran? Did anything come out of this trip on that front?

MYRE: The short answer is no. There's no indication the war, now nearly nine months old, was discussed in any great detail on the trip. Trump did mention it briefly at the news conference. He said what he said many times before - Iran can't have a nuclear weapon and that Iran does want to make a deal. The one significant development in recent days has been increased Iranian attacks on oil tankers and Gulf countries.
body_zh: 特朗普新闻发布会的最新消息 特朗普总统在其历史性的亚洲之行会见了中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京后，举行了一场内容广泛的新闻发布会。
特朗普总统在进行历史性的亚洲之行后举行了内容广泛的新闻发布会，并会见了中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京。
特朗普总统结束为期三天的亚洲之行返回华盛顿，并于今天接受白宫提问。此行包括与中国国家主席习近平和俄罗斯总统普京的首次三方会晤。但在关键的全球问题上几乎没有达成一致。
唐纳德·特朗普总统：美国以无与伦比的经济和外交实力参加此次访问。
张：嗯，所有这些都引发了人们对特朗普美国优先方针的持久力以及美国未来在世界上的角色的质疑。现在加入我们的是 NPR 白宫记者 Franco Ordoñez，他也在房间里，还有 NPR 国家安全记者 Greg Myre。你们俩好。
张：好的。那么，佛朗哥，总统在这次新闻发布会上有透露什么消息吗？
奥多涅斯：是的，我的意思是，不是真的。我的意思是，这确实是一次非常曲折的谈话，从他上任头两年的亮点开始。然后他可能花了大约 30 分钟谈论他在国外的经历，以及你知道的，讲述他与习近平和普京的关系。不过，他确实表示，他和习近平就人工智能（他称之为超级智能）安装​​护栏（这是他用的词）达成了一些协议。他就在那里。
特朗普：这不是人工智能。这不是人工的。太棒了。问题是，它可能太超级了。因此，习主席和我同意，我们两个人要共同做一些护栏，因为真的没有第三个地方。
奥多涅斯：当然，现在细节很少，但护栏的想法值得注意，因为特朗普——至少以前——对发展人工智能的任何限制非常敏感。我的意思是，他一再表示他希望保持美国对中国的优势。
张：对。好吧，格雷格，特朗普对向中国销售芯片以及整个英伟达的影响有一些话要说，对吧？他的回答让你印象深刻的是什么？

MYRE：是的，我的意思是，正如佛朗哥刚刚指出的那样，特朗普表示他希望美国在人工智能领域保持领先地位。他还表示，他不会允许美国公司在美国境外建立人工智能数据中心。然而，特朗普却允许英伟达向中国出售先进芯片。英伟达的黄仁勋去年游说特朗普并说服总统允许这些销售。就在昨天，众议院外交事务委员会公布了英伟达和另一家芯片制造商AMD今年向中国公司出售芯片的请求清单。截至今年5月，特朗普政府已批准销售近90万颗先进芯片，其中包括阿里巴巴和腾讯等大牌企业。这两家公司也在五角大楼列出的与中国军方有联系的中国公司名单上。那么特朗普到底想要什么呢？他是希望英伟达继续向中国销售这些芯片，还是想阻止这些销售？
张：好问题。好吧，特朗普还被问及网络安全领导层的整个变化，对吧？我们在那里学到了什么？
迈尔：是的，特朗普解雇了白宫网络安全总监肖恩·康克罗斯，他在今天的新闻发布会上说，我认为那个人不够好。现在，他被国防部首席信息官克尔斯滕·戴维斯 (Kirsten Davies) 接替。这当然是一个重要的立场，但这是一个政策立场，而不是实际操作立场。

这里真正重要的机构是 CISA，即网络安全和基础设施安全局，负责处理选举安全并保护政府网络免受网络攻击。自特朗普近两年前就任总统以来，该机构一直没有主任。现在，碰巧的是，特朗普提名的该机构负责人迈克尔·洛萨皮奥（Michael LoSapio）昨天在参议院举行了确认听证会。他受到民主党参议员的盘问。他被问到谁赢得了 2020 年总统选举。他拒绝回答。当被问及国会大厦是否在 2021 年 1 月 6 日遭到袭击时，他说他不认为这是一次袭击。因此，尚不清楚他是否会得到确认，但无论谁最终担任这一职务，都将负责 2028 年的选举安全。
张：有趣。好吧，佛朗哥，回到这次与习近平和普京的会面，这次会面的目的是展示美国的实力，对吧？您是否认为这也可能为盟友远离美国打开了大门？
奥尔多内斯：是的，我的意思是，这很大程度上是为了展示美国的实力，但我也认为这确实表明权力和影响力不是同一回事。我的意思是，特朗普今天被问到，他称之为朋友的普京是否也是美国的朋友。
奥尔多内斯：你知道，他真的无法回答这个问题。但他确实继续证明他与普京的关系将为美国带来好处，尽管我们还没有真正看到这一点。要知道，乌克兰战事仍在继续。但我们看到盟友开始与其他国家建立联盟，因为人们对美国的信心动摇，他们希望减少对美国的依赖。
张：嗯，太好了。伊朗问题的进展如何？这次旅行在这方面有什么收获吗？
MYRE：简短的回答是否定的。没有任何迹象表明这次旅行中对已经进行了近九个月的战争进行了任何详细的讨论。特朗普在新闻发布会上确实简短地提到了这一点。他说出了他之前多次说过的话——伊朗不能拥有核武器，而且伊朗确实希望达成协议。最近几天的一项重大进展是伊朗对油轮和海湾国家的袭击有所增加。

title_zh: 特朗普称联邦调查局黑客攻击可能揭露俄罗斯“骗局”
summary: President Trump on Saturday said the reported hack of a crucial FBI database might have a silver lining — it could, he claimed, expose more details of what he called the " Russia Russia Russia hoax ." Why it matters: The president remains laser-focused on many
summary_zh: 特朗普总统周六表示，据报道，联邦调查局一个重要数据库遭到黑客攻击可能有一线希望——他声称，这可能会暴露更多细节
body_en: President Trump on Saturday said the reported hack of a crucial FBI database might have a silver lining — it could, he claimed, expose more details of what he called the " Russia Russia Russia hoax ."
Why it matters: The president remains laser-focused on many of his past grievances about the FBI , even as the public grows increasingly alarmed about the vulnerability of government infrastructure.

Driving the news: CNN and NBC reported Friday night that the FBI was looking into an apparent breach of the National Crime Information Center, which connects local and national law enforcement for information sharing.
That follows breaches and outages that struck the FAA, NSA and USDA, just in the last week.
What they're saying: Trump was asked about the FBI reports in a Fox News interview Saturday morning.
"Well we just heard about it and I will say that it's not good, I don't like that," Trump said.
"But maybe we'll learn things that we would have never learned otherwise. You had the Russia Russia Russia hoax, you had all these other hoaxes," he added, referring to Ukraine in particular.
"Maybe we'll learn about them. Maybe we'll learn about the voter fraud, all the voter fraud that took place."
"I always like to put things in a positive spin," Trump added.
"Wouldn't it be great to learn about Russia Russia Russia," he said.
The intrigue: The president's comments come just days after a summit with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Asia, after which he described Putin as a " friend ."
What to watch: It's not clear who breached the FBI database, or what they might do with the data obtained.
body_zh: 特朗普总统周六表示，据报道，联邦调查局重要数据库遭到黑客攻击可能有一线希望——他声称，这可能会暴露他所谓的“俄罗斯俄罗斯骗局”的更多细节。
为什么重要：尽管公众对政府基础设施的脆弱性越来越感到担忧，但总统仍然专注于他过去对联邦调查局的许多不满。
推动新闻发展：美国有线电视新闻网 (CNN) 和全国广播公司 (NBC) 周五晚间报道称，联邦调查局 (FBI) 正在调查国家犯罪信息中心的明显违规行为，该中心连接地方和国家执法部门以实现信息共享。
就在上周，美国联邦航空管理局、美国国家安全局和美国农业部都发生了违规和中断事件。
他们说的是：特朗普在周六早上接受福克斯新闻采访时被问及联邦调查局的报告。
特朗普说：“我们刚刚听说这件事，我会说这不好，我不喜欢这样。”
“但也许我们会学到一些我们永远不会学到的东西。你有俄罗斯俄罗斯骗局，你有所有这些其他骗局，”他补充说，特别是指乌克兰。
“也许我们会了解他们。也许我们会了解选民欺诈，所有发生的选民欺诈。”
特朗普补充道：“我总是喜欢让事情往积极的方向发展。”
“了解俄罗斯俄罗斯俄罗斯不是很棒吗？”他说。
阴谋：总统在与俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京和中国领导人习近平在亚洲举行峰会几天后发表了上述言论，峰会后他将普京描述为“朋友”。
看点：目前尚不清楚是谁破坏了联邦调查局的数据库，也不清楚他们可能会如何处理所获得的数据。

title_en: New Democratic governors race to deliver relief on costs
title_zh: 新民主党州长竞相减轻成本
summary: The newly elected state executives are plotting solutions on health care, housing and energy.
summary_zh: 新当选的州政府官员正在制定医疗保健、住房和能源方面的解决方案。
body_en: PARK CITY, Utah — Cost-of-living concerns fueled Democrats to victory this month. Now they’re preparing to do something about it.

As newly elected governors gathered for a job training conference hosted by the National Governors Association, conversations among the Democrat-heavy group often turned to the economic woes in their states — and the necessity to get something done quickly.

“What are the things that we can do — not in the first 100 days, but in the first 100 hours — that can start bringing some relief to the American people?” Wes Moore, the National Governors Association chair and Maryland governor, said in an interview with POLITICO.

Health care and home costs topped the target list. Several newly elected Democratic governors — Jocelyn Benson in Michigan, Keisha Lance Bottoms in Georgia, Deb Haaland in New Mexico and Rob Sand in Iowa — plan to take action to lower health costs, ranging from caps on prescription drug prices to expanding Medicaid coverage, within days of taking office. California Gov.-elect Xavier Becerra promised to spur affordable housing construction. His Nevada counterpart, Aaron Ford, said he plans to limit corporations purchasing private homes, and is preparing a day-one executive order to task every state agency with “finding ways to put money back in people's pockets.”

“You hear people signing executive orders to make things easier for businesses, cut regulations, and make it easier to do business. I think that's cool, that's fine, that's dandy,” Ford said in an interview. “But if you can do it for businesses, you can do it for people, too.”

Affordability was, far and away, the top issue for voters this cycle. Results from The POLITICO Poll, conducted just days after the midterm elections, found a 47% plurality of Americans — including 59% of Democratic voters and 41% of Republicans — said affordability and the economy were among the main issues driving their vote.

Democrats’ tsunami washed over governors’ mansions across the nation: They won 24 of the 36 governor’s races held this month, flipping red states like Texas, Alaska and Ohio, and will hold 30 of the 50 governorships nationwide next year — the most in three decades.

These governors and soon-to-be governors will be buoyed by a boon of Democrats in their statehouses: Democrats won unified control of government in Michigan, Minnesota, Nevada and Wisconsin; in North Carolina, Democrats flipped the House for the first time in 16 years and broke Republicans’ supermajority in the Senate.

As several inches of snow descended on the Wasatch Front and blanketed the glitzy ski resort in Park City this week, the newly elected governors sheltered inside the NGA’s New Governors Leadership Forum — colloquially called “baby governors’ school.” At the two-day seminar, the incoming state executives and their teams attended seminars and workshops, mingled over hors d'oeuvres and heard from current and former governors on what to expect.

Former President Bill Clinton, sitting spread-legged in a Team USA sweater Thursday, dished to a room full of governors on his book recommendations (“The Social Conquest of Earth” by E.O. Wilson), fun facts (“The combined weight of ants on earth exceeds the combined weight of all the people on earth!”) and political predictions (“I think if President Trump gets closer to leaving, he may get more interested in leaving actual legacies in forms other than buildings.”)

Clinton, who chaired the NGA when he served as governor of Arkansas, also offered some advice to the newly electeds: “The most important thing is that you and your Cabinet and your office and your organizations out in the state know what your priorities are and know what your progress is.”

Governors will face a steep climb to deliver immediate relief to Americans. Economic forces are national and international, and much of the past year’s price spikes, from fuel to food to energy, can be tied to the Iran war.

Bottoms said she will immediately begin to prepare Georgia agencies for Medicaid expansion, and expects the state legislature — with Democrats now in control of the state House, while Republicans still control the state Senate — to cooperate.
“I do believe this is an issue we will get bipartisan support on,” she told POLITICO.

In addition to his Day-One executive order, Ford says he plans to work with the Nevada legislature to sign bills in his first 30 days on expanding free public school meals, lowering the cost of prescription drugs to the Medicaid negotiated price and limiting corporations’ ability to buy private homes.

Benson said she has already reached out to the Trump administration about tariffs, which includes a 50% tariff on most Canadian exports and have disproportionately impacted Michiganders. She said she has not yet heard back, but “the point is I have reached out, and I do hope to have that conversation.”
She also emphasized her focus on lowering health care costs. “That's life or death for so many families,” Benson said.
Megan Messerly and Adam Wren contributed reporting.
body_zh: 犹他州帕克城——对生活成本的担忧促使民主党在本月取得胜利。现在他们正准备对此采取行动。
当新当选的州长聚集在一起参加由全国州长协会主办的职业培训会议时，以民主党为主的团体之间的谈话经常转向本州的经济困境，以及迅速完成某些事情的必要性。
“我们可以做哪些事情——不是在前 100 天，而是在前 100 小时——可以开始为美国人民带来一些缓解？”全国州长协会主席、马里兰州州长韦斯·摩尔在接受《POLITICO》采访时表示。

医疗保健和家庭费用位居目标清单之首。几位新当选的民主党州长——密歇根州的乔斯林·本森、佐治亚州的凯莎·兰斯·博顿斯、新墨西哥州的德布·哈兰德和爱荷华州的罗布·桑德——计划在上任后几天内采取行动降低医疗成本，从处方药价格上限到扩大医疗补助覆盖范围。当选加州州长泽维尔·贝塞拉承诺刺激经济适用房建设。内华达州同行亚伦·福特表示，他计划限制企业购买私人住宅，并正在准备一项第一天的行政命令，要求每个州机构“想办法让钱回到人们的口袋里”。
“你会听到人们签署行政命令，让企业变得更容易，减少监管，让做生意更容易。我认为这很酷，很好，这太棒了，”福特在接受采访时说。 “但如果你能为企业做到这一点，你也可以为人们做到这一点。”
负担能力无疑是本周期选民的首要问题。中期选举几天后进行的 POLITICO 民意调查显示，47% 的美国人（包括 59% 的民主党选民和 41% 的共和党选民）表示，负担能力和经济是推动他们投票的主要问题之一。
民主党的海啸席卷了全国各地的州长官邸：他们赢得了本月举行的 36 场州长竞选中的 24 场，击败了得克萨斯州、阿拉斯加州和俄亥俄州等红州，并将在明年获得全国 50 个州长职位中的 30 个——这是三十年来最多的一次。
这些州长和即将上任的州长将受到州议会中民主党人的支持：民主党赢得了密歇根州、明尼苏达州、内华达州和威斯康星州政府的统一控制权；民主党赢得了密歇根州、明尼苏达州、内华达州和威斯康星州的政府统一控制权；在北卡罗来纳州，民主党16年来首次翻转众议院，打破了共和党在参议院的绝对多数席位。
本周，瓦萨奇前线降下数英寸厚的积雪，覆盖了帕克城华丽的滑雪胜地，新当选的州长们躲在 NGA 的新州长领导力论坛（俗称“婴儿州长学校”）内。在为期两天的研讨会上，即将上任的州行政人员及其团队参加了研讨会和讲习班，一边享用开胃小菜，一边听取现任和前任州长的意见。
周四，前总统比尔·克林顿穿着美国队毛衣，张开双腿坐着，向满屋子的州长推荐他的书籍（E.O.威尔逊的《社会征服地球》）、有趣的事实（“地球上蚂蚁的总重量超过了地球上所有人的总重量！”）和政治预测（“我认为，如果特朗普总统离任越来越近，他可能会对以建筑物以外的形式留下实际遗产更感兴趣。”）
担任阿肯色州州长期间担任 NGA 主席的克林顿也向新当选的人提出了一些建议：“最重要的是，你和你的内阁、你的办公室以及你在该州的组织知道你的优先事项是什么，知道你的进展是什么。”
州长们将面临陡峭的攀升，以立即为美国人提供救济。经济力量是国内和国际的，去年从燃料到食品再到能源的价格上涨大部分都与伊朗战争有关。
博托姆斯表示，她将立即开始为佐治亚州各机构扩大医疗补助计划做好准备，并预计州立法机构（目前民主党控制着州众议院，而共和党仍控制着州参议院）进行合作。
“我确实相信这是一个我们会得到两党支持的问题，”她告诉《政治》杂志。
福特表示，除了第一天的行政命令外，他还计划在上任后的 30 天内与内华达州立法机构合作签署法案，扩大公立学校的免费餐食，将处方药的成本降低至医疗补助协议的谈判价格，并限制企业购买私人住宅的能力。
本森表示，她已经就关税问题与特朗普政府进行了接触，其中包括对大多数加拿大出口产品征收 50% 的关税，这对密歇根人造成了不成比例的影响。她说她还没有收到回复，但“重点是我已经联系了，我确实希望进行对话。”
她还强调了她对降低医疗保健成本的关注。 “这对许多家庭来说是生死攸关的事情，”本森说。
梅根·梅瑟利和亚当·雷恩贡献了报道。

title_en: Virginia child dies in state’s first measles-associated death of 2026
title_zh: 弗吉尼亚州一名儿童死于该州 2026 年首例麻疹相关死亡
summary: Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state
summary_zh: 死亡加剧了全国麻疹疫情，在弗吉尼亚州报告首例麻疹 26 年后，美国最近失去了麻疹消除地位
body_en: Death adds to national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years
Virginia reported its first measles-associated death of 2026 ⁠on Friday, involving a child who tested positive for the infectious disease, the state’s health department said.
The department said the child was ⁠age four or younger. It did not disclose additional details, including the child’s vaccination status, citing the family’s privacy.
The death adds to a worsening national measles outbreak that recently cost the US its measles elimination status after 26 years.
US loses measles elimination status amid worst outbreak since 1991
Pennsylvania, the hardest-hit US state, reported an eighth measles-related death and confirmed 1,631 measles cases as of Friday.
Wisconsin has ⁠also reported two deaths, while New York state recorded its first measles-associated ​death, involving a ​child.
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) has confirmed six ​measles-associated deaths so far in 2026, though it does not ​specify the states ‌where the deaths were ​recorded.

A discrepancy between ​state and federal death tallies arose after the CDC, under the Trump administration’s health secretary, Robert F Kennedy Jr, began using National Center for Health Statistics mortality data instead of state figures.
Virginia has reported 220 measles ⁠cases so far in 2026, including 40 among children four years old or younger and 75 among those age five to 12, state ⁠health department data showed as of Thursday.
Of those cases, 179 involved unvaccinated individuals, 39 were associated with people ‌whose vaccination status was ‌unknown and two occurred with vaccinated individuals.

“Virginia has not had a measles-related death ‌since 1978,” said Frederic Bertley, immunologist and chief executive officer of the Center of Science and Industry. Bertley added that the measles virus infection is both alarming and evidence that measles is gaining a foothold and becoming a growing problem for the US.

Virginia health officials have reported increased measles activity driven largely by outbreaks ‌in the state’s central region. Buckingham county has reported 127 cases, the most in the state, while neighboring Charlotte county has recorded 34 ​cases.
body_zh: 死亡事件加剧了全国麻疹疫情，最近使美国在 26 年后失去了消除麻疹的地位
弗吉尼亚州卫生部门表示，该州周五报告了 2026 年首例与麻疹相关的死亡，其中一名儿童的传染病检测结果呈阳性。
该部门表示，该孩子年龄四岁或更小。它以家庭隐私为由，没有透露更多细节，包括孩子的疫苗接种情况。
这起死亡事件加剧了全国麻疹疫情的恶化，最近使美国失去了 26 年后的麻疹消除状态。
由于1991年以来最严重的麻疹疫情，美国失去了消除麻疹的地位
美国受灾最严重的州宾夕法尼亚州报告了第八例与麻疹相关的死亡病例，截至周五，该州确诊了 1,631 例麻疹病例。
威斯康星州还报告了两例死亡，而纽约州则记录了首例与麻疹相关的死亡，涉及一名儿童。
美国疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 已确认 2026 年迄今为止有 6 例与麻疹相关的死亡，但没有具体说明死亡记录在哪个州。
在特朗普政府卫生部长小罗伯特·F·肯尼迪领导下的疾病预防控制中心开始使用国家卫生统计中心的死亡率数据而不是州数据后，州和联邦的死亡统计数据出现了差异。
截至周四，州卫生部门的数据显示，弗吉尼亚州截至 2026 年已报告 220 例麻疹病例，其中 40 例为四岁或以下儿童，75 例为 5 至 12 岁儿童。
在这些病例中，179 例涉及未接种疫苗的人，39 例涉及疫苗接种状况未知的人，两例涉及已接种疫苗的人。
“自 1978 年以来，弗吉尼亚州没有出现过与麻疹相关的死亡，”免疫学家兼科学与工业中心首席执行官弗雷德里克·伯特利 (Frederic Bertley) 说。伯特利补充说，麻疹病毒感染既令人震惊，也有证据表明麻疹正在站稳脚跟，并成为美国面临的一个日益严重的问题。
弗吉尼亚州卫生官员报告说，麻疹活动增加主要是由于该州中部地区的疫情爆发所致。白金汉县已报告 127 例病例，为该州最多，而邻近的夏洛特县已报告 34 例。

title_en: A second judge blocks Trump's arch, saying it's unlikely to succeed in court
title_zh: 第二名法官挡住了特朗普的拱门，称其不太可能在法庭上成功
summary: A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
summary_zh: 弗吉尼亚州的一名联邦法官表示，她将针对特朗普的拱门发布初步禁令，这比华盛顿特区的联邦法官更进一步。
body_en: Trump arch blocked by Virginia judge A federal judge in Virginia said she will issue a preliminary injunction against Trump's arch, going a step further than the D.C. federal judge who temporarily blocked construction earlier this week.
President Trump holds up a model of his proposed triumphal arch at a White House event in Oct. 2025. Two different federal judges have ruled against it this week. John McDonnell/AP hide caption
A federal judge in Virginia plans to issue a preliminary injunction blocking President Trump's triumphal arch indefinitely.

District Judge Leonie Brinkema said during a Friday hearing that she would grant the request of the county board of Arlington, Va., which sued over the arch in October. Democracy Forward, the nonprofit representing the plaintiffs, confirmed the ruling in a statement shared with NPR.
Judges have put Trump's arch and golf course on hold, but only for a matter of days

"We are pleased that the court has recognized the irreparable harm that will come to people who live and work in Arlington and stopped the massive vanity project while our case is heard and considered by the court," said senior counsel Kate Talmor.
Justice Department spokesperson Matthew Nies told NPR it will appeal the decision immediately.

The 250-foot arch would be built in Memorial Circle, which is part of D.C. but sits on the Virginia side of the Potomac River, a short distance from both Arlington National Cemetery and Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport, both in Arlington.

Arlington County has argued that the arch would "cause significant harm" to its residents in multiple ways, including increasing noise and air pollution and "clogging thoroughfares needed for emergency transport services." And it said an arch that doubles as a military complex — as Trump has suggested — would pose public safety risks and require additional county resources to manage.

Arlington also argues the arch would disrupt historic sightlines between Arlington National Cemetery and D.C.'s National Mall , and pose logistical challenges for the roughly 24 to 27 funerals the cemetery holds every weekday. The county also has concerns about air and road traffic, saying construction-related delays could cause more accidents and disrupt emergency vehicles far beyond the traffic circle.

"In the last 60 days, Arlington police, fire, and emergency units have responded to approximately 200 incidents in the area surrounding the Circle, including traffic stops and assisting with unconscious persons within Arlington National Cemetery," they wrote. "And the visitors the Arch is intended to attract will increase demand for those same emergency services."
Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave

The plaintiffs, like many critics of the arch , accused the Trump administration of rushing through federally mandated environmental reviews and failing to consider alternatives. The National Park Service has defended the federal review process — which ended in approval earlier this month — and said building the arch somewhere else would defeat its purpose .

"The County brings this lawsuit to halt the agency's feverish pace toward construction of the Arch and to ensure that the 'hard look' mandated by [the National Environmental Preservation Act] is completed before the agency commences disruptive and harmful ground-disturbing activities," the plaintiffs wrote last month.

NPR has reached out to the White House for comment. Spokesperson Davis Ingle told NPR earlier this week that the administration will "continue making the case for this beautiful and fitting monument and are confident we will be fully vindicated as this litigation proceeds."
Brinkema, an appointee of President Clinton, is the second judge to rule against the arch this week.

On Wednesday, D.C. District Judge Tanya Chutkan extended a restraining order that prevents the Trump administration from breaking ground through Dec. 3 while she considers the underlying legal arguments.
Democrats want to stop Trump's arch, golf course and more. What are their options?

That case was brought earlier this year by a group that includes Vietnam War veterans and was joined by the governments of D.C. and Virginia last month. Nine Kennedy family members moved to get involved last week.
body_zh: 弗吉尼亚州法官封锁特朗普拱门 弗吉尼亚州一名联邦法官表示，她将对特朗普拱门发布初步禁令，这比本周早些时候暂时阻止施工的华盛顿特区联邦法官更进一步。
特朗普总统在 2025 年 10 月的白宫活动中举起了他提议的凯旋门模型。本周，两名不同的联邦法官做出了反对的裁决。约翰·麦克唐纳/美联社隐藏标题栏
弗吉尼亚州的一名联邦法官计划发布初步禁令，无限期阻止特朗普总统的凯旋门。
地区法官莱昂妮·布林克玛 (Leonie Brinkema) 在周五的听证会上表示，她将批准弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿县委员会的请求，该县委员会于 10 月份就拱门提起了诉讼。代表原告的非营利组织“民主前进”在与 NPR 分享的一份声明中证实了这一裁决。
法官暂停了特朗普的拱门和高尔夫球场，但只持续了几天
高级律师凯特·塔尔莫 (Kate Talmor) 表示：“我们很高兴法院认识到这将对阿灵顿生活和工作的人们造成不可挽回的伤害，并在法院审理和审议我们的案件期间停止了大规模的虚荣工程。”
司法部发言人马修·尼斯 (Matthew Nies) 告诉 NPR，司法部将立即对这一决定提出上诉。
这座 250 英尺高的拱门将建在纪念圆环内，该纪念环是华盛顿特区的一部分，但位于波托马克河的弗吉尼亚一侧，距离阿灵顿国家公墓和罗纳德·里根华盛顿国家机场都很近。
阿灵顿县辩称，这座拱门将以多种方式对其居民“造成重大伤害”，包括增加噪音和空气污染以及“堵塞紧急交通服务所需的通道”。它还表示，正如特朗普所建议的那样，一座兼作军事设施的拱门将构成公共安全风险，并需要额外的县资源来管理。
阿灵顿还认为，这座拱门会扰乱阿灵顿国家公墓和华盛顿特区国家广场之间的历史视线，并给该公墓每周举办大约 24 至 27 场葬礼带来后勤挑战。该县还对空中和道路交通表示担忧，称与施工相关的延误可能会导致更多事故，并扰乱远离交通圈的紧急车辆。
他们写道：“在过去 60 天里，阿灵顿警察、消防和应急部门对圆环周边地区约 ​​200 起事件做出了反应，包括在阿灵顿国家公墓内拦截交通并协助失去知觉的人员。” “拱门旨在吸引的游客将增加对这些紧急服务的需求。”
肯尼迪亲属加入反对特朗普拱门的斗争，声称肯尼迪坟墓遭到破坏
与许多对该拱门的批评者一样，原告指责特朗普政府匆忙进行联邦政府规定的环境审查，而没有考虑替代方案。国家公园管理局为联邦审查程序进行了辩护——该程序于本月初获得批准——并表示在其他地方建造拱门将达不到其目的。
原告上个月写道：“县提起这起诉讼是为了阻止该机构建造拱门的狂热步伐，并确保在该机构开始破坏性和有害的地面扰动活动之前完成[国家环境保护法]规定的‘严格审查’。”
NPR 已联系白宫请其置评。发言人戴维斯·英格尔本周早些时候告诉美国公共广播电台，政府将“继续为这座美丽而合适的纪念碑辩护，并相信随着诉讼的进行，我们将得到充分证明。”
克林顿总统任命的布林克马是本周第二位做出反对拱门裁决的法官。
周三，华盛顿地区法官塔尼娅·查特坎 (Tanya Chutkan) 延长了一项限制令，阻止特朗普政府在 12 月 3 日之前破土动工，同时她正在考虑潜在的法律论据。
民主党人希望阻止特朗普的拱门、高尔夫球场等。他们的选择是什么？
今年早些时候，一个包括越南战争退伍军人在内的团体提起了这一诉讼，上个月华盛顿特区和弗吉尼亚州政府也加入了该诉讼。肯尼迪家族的九名成员上周也参与其中。

title_en: Witness recounts a botched execution in Texas: ‘Just such horror and terror and pain’
title_zh: 目击者讲述了德克萨斯州一次拙劣的处决：“真是太恐怖、恐怖和痛苦”
summary: Rev Dr Jeff Hood stood at the side of Reinaldo Dennes as the state of Texas put him to death, calling the experience ‘overwhelming’ “Take me, father!” It was one of many cries Reinaldo Dennes uttered on Thursday night as he lay strapped to a gurney inside a Te
summary_zh: 当德克萨斯州处决雷纳尔多·丹尼斯时，杰夫·胡德牧师站在他身边，称这次经历“令人难以承受”，“父亲，带我去吧！”
body_en: Rev Dr Jeff Hood stood at the side of Reinaldo Dennes as the state of Texas put him to death, calling the experience ‘overwhelming’

It was one of many cries Reinaldo Dennes uttered on Thursday night as he lay strapped to a gurney inside a Texas death chamber while prison officials struggled, for more than an hour, to carry out his execution .

Rev Dr Jeff Hood, Dennes’s spiritual adviser, stood by his side, his hand resting on the condemned man’s shoulder throughout the lethal injection, a procedure that witnesses agreed went terribly wrong.
“The energy that was coming off of him was just such horror and terror and pain, it was overwhelming,” Hood said on Friday morning.

Dennes’s was the 15th execution Hood has witnessed. A prominent advocate against capital punishment, the reverend regularly serves as a spiritual leader for people on death row across the US, offering guidance in the prisoners’ final months – and at times, holding them in their final minutes. Thirteen of those executions were lethal injections.
Dennes’s procedure, Hood said, was the worst lethal injection he’s witnessed – by far.

Before Thursday, Dennes, 70, had spent three decades on death row, sentenced to capital punishment for the 1996 murder of Janos Szucs, a diamond dealer. In the weeks leading up to his scheduled killing, Dennes was at peace, said Hood.
“He was borderline euphoric about dying – he was so excited about getting out of prison and meeting God,” Hood said. “In the waiting cell, he said: ‘Don’t be sad. This is great. I’m going home.’”

After nearby church bells rang at 6pm, officials escorted witnesses into the Huntsville unit, a Texas prison opened in 1849. In typical Texas executions, witnesses would be brought into the death chamber soon after, after the prisoner was strapped down and an intravenous line was established. But on Thursday, they were left waiting. And waiting.

Hood said he knew something was wrong. Officials, he presumed, were probably having difficulties establishing the IV line to administer pentobarbital, a lethal sedative. Executioners across the country have had similar struggles , including the botched, failed execution of Christa Pike in Tennessee in September.
After roughly 30 minutes, the witnesses were brought into the execution room. Hood saw IV lines had been placed into Dennes’s neck and foot.

Hood lay his hand on Dennes’s shoulder, he recalled. He told Dennes how much he loved him and thanked him for their friendship. In his final remarks, Dennes said he was “extremely blessed”, according to the Associated Press’s account , and that he hoped his family members “get to know this great gift and great grace of God the father”.
The reverend recalled that Dennes signaled he was ready to proceed, calling out: “Go, warden!”
The pentobarbital started to flow at 6.52pm, according to a prison spokesperson .
Officials have said the drug should quickly render people unconscious. Hood previously witnessed three lethal injections in Texas and said those procedures had occurred “without a hitch”.
Dennes’s body began to heave under Hood’s hand, he said.
“He’s still shifting, he’s still moving, he’s pulling on the leather straps, and I can feel his shoulder pushing into my palm,” Hood said. Dennes, he said, felt like a “bucking bronco”.
Dennes cried out, “My leg, my leg! … [It’s] killing me,” yelling that it felt as if he was on fire, according to Hood.

For several minutes, Dennes’s cries continued, shouting, “Fuck! Fuck!” and “Shit!”, Hood said. The fact that he was able to utter any words after a minute was extremely distressing, Hood said, and it was soon clear that he was begging for it to end.
body_zh: 当德克萨斯州处决雷纳尔多·丹尼斯时，杰夫·胡德牧师站在他一边，称这次经历“令人难以承受”
这是雷纳尔多·丹尼斯周四晚上发出的众多呼喊之一，当时他被绑在得克萨斯州死刑室内的轮床上，而监狱官员在一个多小时的时间里奋力执行他的死刑。
丹尼斯的精神顾问杰夫·胡德牧师博士站在他的身边，在注射死刑的整个过程中，他的手放在死刑犯的肩膀上，目击者一致认为，这一程序是错误的。
“他身上散发出的能量是如此恐怖、恐惧和痛苦，令人难以承受，”胡德周五早上说道。
丹尼斯的处决是胡德目睹的第 15 次处决。这位牧师是反对死刑的著名倡导者，经常担任美国各地死囚的精神领袖，为囚犯的最后几个月提供指导，有时甚至在他们生命的最后几分钟陪伴他们。其中 13 次处决是注射死刑。
胡德说，丹尼斯的注射死刑是迄今为止他所见过的最严重的注射死刑。
周四之前，70 岁的丹尼斯因 1996 年谋杀钻石经销商亚诺什·苏克斯 (Janos Szucs) 被判处死刑，已在死囚牢房里度过了三十年的时光。胡德说，在预定的杀戮前几周，丹尼斯很平静。
“他对死亡感到欣喜若狂——他对出狱并见到上帝感到非常兴奋，”胡德说。 “在候诊室里，他说：‘别伤心。这太棒了。我要回家了。’”
下午 6 点附近教堂的钟声响起后，官员们护送证人进入德克萨斯州亨茨维尔监狱，这是一所于 1849 年启用的监狱。在典型的德克萨斯州处决中，在囚犯被绑起来并建立静脉注射管后不久，证人就会被带入死刑室。但到了周四，他们却只能等待。等待。
胡德说他知道出了什么问题。他推测，官员们可能在建立注射戊巴比妥（一种致命镇静剂）的静脉注射管线时遇到了困难。全国各地的刽子手都经历过类似的挣扎，包括九月在田纳西州对克里斯塔·派克的处决，但处理得很糟糕，失败了。
大约30分钟后，目击者被带入行刑室。胡德看到丹尼斯的脖子和脚上已经插入了静脉注射线。
胡德回忆道，他把手放在丹尼斯的肩膀上。他告诉丹尼斯他有多么爱他，并感谢他的友谊。据美联社报道，丹尼斯在最后致辞中表示，他“非常幸运”，并希望他的家人“了解天父上帝的这份伟大礼物和伟大恩典”。
牧师回忆说，丹尼斯示意他准备好继续前进，并喊道：“走吧，典狱长！”
据监狱发言人称，戊巴比妥于下午 6 点 52 分开始流动。
官员们表示，这种药物应该会很快使人失去知觉。胡德此前曾在德克萨斯州目睹过三起注射死刑事件，并表示这些程序“顺利”进行。
丹尼斯说，他的身体开始在胡德的手下起伏。
“他仍在移动，他仍在移动，他拉着皮带，我能感觉到他的肩膀推入我的手掌，”胡德说。他说，丹尼斯感觉就像一匹“狂野的野马”。
据胡德说，丹尼斯喊道，“我的腿，我的腿！……（它）要了我的命”，他大喊着，感觉自己好像着火了。
几分钟后，丹尼斯的哭声一直持续着，喊道：“操！操！”胡德说：“妈的！”胡德说，一分钟后他就能够说出任何话，这一事实令人极其痛苦，而且很快就很明显他正在乞求这一切结束。

title_en: ‘Hell dorm’: Florida prisoners testify about 119F heat indexes and walls that sweat
title_zh: “地狱宿舍”：佛罗里达囚犯证实 119 华氏度的高温和出汗的墙壁
summary: Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced
summary_zh: 囚犯称，周二下午，德韦恩·威尔逊 (Dwayne Wilson) 称，混凝土设施中的高温导致一名男子因呼吸困难而死亡。
body_en: Temperatures in a concrete facility contributed to one man’s death after he struggled to breathe, prisoners allege

On Tuesday afternoon Dwayne Wilson, 69, a thin Black man dressed in a light gray prison uniform, testified about the stifling heat he experienced in the Dade correctional institute, a concrete state prison south of Miami, Florida , without air conditioning. He removed his glasses and wiped his eyes as he spoke. “It was so hot,” he said, his voice catching. “It’s so hot sometimes you have to put water on the floor just to try to keep cool.”

Wilson said he’s housed in the H dorms, a T-shaped building with one-to-two-person cells, nicknamed “hell dorm” by prisoners because its concrete walls radiate heat absorbed from the sun. The plaintiff’s law firm, the Florida Justice Institute , convinced a judge to allow 31 sensors to be temporarily installed throughout the prison during the summer of 2025. They recorded temperature and humidity levels that Stefano Shiavon , a professor of civil and environmental engineering with expertise in thermal comfort, used to calculate the heat index. He found it to be above 88F (31C) 97% of the time, with the highest heat indexes often recorded at night, including one reading in the H dorm dayroom equivalent to 119F (48C) at 10pm one July day last year. “The walls sweat,” Wilson said. “It’s miserable in the cell at night because, again, it’s so hot. No air comes to the bed we sleep at and the bed is soaked in sweat.”
body_zh: 囚犯称，混凝土设施中的温度导致一名男子呼吸困难后死亡
周二下午，69 岁的德韦恩·威尔逊 (Dwayne Wilson) 是一名身着浅灰色囚服的瘦瘦黑人，他作证称，他在戴德惩教所 (佛罗里达州迈阿密以南的一所混凝土州立监狱，没有空调) 中经历了令人窒息的高温。他边说边摘下眼镜，擦了擦眼睛。 “天气太热了，”他说道，声音很沙哑。 “天气太热了，有时你不得不在地板上泼水才能保持凉爽。”

威尔逊说，他被安置在 H 宿舍里，这是一栋 T 形建筑，里面有一到两人的牢房，囚犯们戏称“地狱宿舍”，因为它的混凝土墙会散发从太阳吸收的热量。原告的律师事务所佛罗里达司法研究所说服法官允许在 2025 年夏季在整个监狱临时安装 31 个传感器。他们记录了温度和湿度水平，具有热舒适专业知识的土木与环境工程教授 Stefano Shiavon 用来计算炎热指数。他发现 97% 的时间温度都在 88 华氏度（31 摄氏度）以上，最高热指数经常在夜间记录，包括去年 7 月的一天晚上 10 点在 H 宿舍日间的读数相当于 119 华氏度（48 摄氏度）。 “墙壁出汗了，”威尔逊说。 “晚上在牢房里很痛苦，因为又太热了。我们睡觉的床上没有空气，床被汗水浸湿了。”

title_en: Trump initially accepted the midterm results, but most GOP voters doubt they were fair
title_zh: 特朗普最初接受了中期结果，但大多数共和党选民怀疑这些结果是否公平
summary: Less than half of Republicans nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling.
summary_zh: 根据新的民意调查，全国不到一半的共和党人认为中期选举“自由和公平”。
body_en: A firefighter walks past voting booths at a firehouse serving as a polling location in Detroit on Nov. 3. Spencer Platt/Getty Images hide caption
President Trump may have initially accepted the results of his party's midterm losses , but data released Friday shows there is still broad distrust in the elections process among Republicans.

Less than half of Republican voters nationwide considered the midterm elections "free and fair," according to new polling by the University of California San Diego. Just 52% of Republicans said they trusted votes were counted accurately.
In comparison, after the 2024 election that Trump won, more than 80% of Republicans said they had confidence in the vote-counting process.
While trust in elections often dips for voters of the losing party, the GOP has seen bigger swings in confidence in recent years, as Trump has falsely claimed that U.S. elections are corrupt.

"There are still a lot of people who remain unconvinced that they can trust elections," said Thad Kousser, a co-director of UC San Diego's Center for Transparent and Trusted Elections. "And they're predominantly located in one [political] party."

Overall, a wide majority — 66% — of Americans said they think the midterms were fair. That represents an improvement from before the election , when less than half of U.S. adults said they expected free and fair contests.

But that post-election increase in trust was buoyed by Democrats and independents — many of whom worried before Election Day about potential federal interference at the polls that didn't come to pass .

"It would be a mistake to [look at the 66%] and think, 'Oh, everyone has a pretty good view of the election,'" said Lauren Prather, also a co-director of UC San Diego's election center. "It really buries the lede a little bit about the partisan gap."
GOP state officials push to revive Trump's mail voting restrictions for 2028 election
The Trump administration's voter roll crusade could continue
The widespread doubt among Republicans may be a reality check for those wondering whether Trump's brand of election denial has run its course in American politics.

On the one hand, there will be fewer politicians who deny or question election results in office next year. And the vast majority of election-denying candidates running for positions involved in overseeing statewide elections lost their races this year, according to tracking by the advocacy group States United Action.
Election experts have also celebrated as Trump and high-profile losing candidates on the ballot this year conceded their losses.
"Sure, I'll accept [the results]," Trump told Fox News' Bret Baier on election night, as it became clear Democrats would retake the House and Senate. "Why wouldn't I?"
But just a few days later, he began conspiracy theorizing about those same results.
"Does anybody really believe that this 'Election' was honest," Trump posted online .

The new polling from UC San Diego shows that among Republicans, there still may be a receptive audience to such claims. When asked if politicians are discussing voter fraud too much, too little or about the right amount, just 15% of Republicans answered "too much."

"There is both demand among the Republican base for continued focus on this issue, and as we saw even after the election, politicians are continuing to supply it," Kousser said. "As long as those two dynamics are there, there's still going to be a market for these concerns."
body_zh: 11 月 3 日，底特律，一名消防员走过作为投票地点的消防站的投票站。Spencer Platt/Getty Images 隐藏标题栏
特朗普总统最初可能已经接受了本党中期选举失利的结果，但周五公布的数据显示，共和党人对选举进程仍存在广泛的不信任。
根据加州大学圣地亚哥分校的最新民意调查，全国不到一半的共和党选民认为中期选举“自由和公平”。只有 52% 的共和党人表示，他们相信计票结果是准确的。
相比之下，特朗普赢得2024年大选后，超过80%的共和党人表示对计票过程有信心。
虽然失败政党的选民对选举的信任度经常下降，但近年来共和党的信心波动更大，因为特朗普错误地声称美国选举存在腐败。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校透明和可信选举中心联席主任萨德·库塞尔表示：“仍然有很多人不相信选举可以信任。” “而且他们主要属于一个[政治]政党。”
总体而言，绝大多数（66%）美国人表示，他们认为中期选举是公平的。这比选举前有所改善，当时不到一半的美国成年人表示他们期待自由和公平的竞争。
但选举后信任度的提高得到了民主党人和独立人士的提振——他们中的许多人在选举日之前担心联邦可能对民意调查进行干预，但这种干预并未实现。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校选举中心联合主任劳伦·普拉瑟 (Lauren Prather) 表示：“（看看 66% 的人）并认为‘哦，每个人都对选举有很好的看法’，这是错误的。” “这确实掩盖了一些关于党派分歧的争论。”
共和党州官员推动恢复特朗普对 2028 年大选的邮件投票限制
特朗普政府的选民名册运动可能会继续
共和党人普遍存在的疑虑可能是对那些想知道特朗普否认选举的做法是否已经在美国政治中走到尽头的人们的现实检验。
一方面，明年在任时否认或质疑选举结果的政客将会减少。根据倡导组织“联合行动”的追踪，绝大多数竞选参与监督全州选举职位的拒绝选举的候选人今年都输掉了竞选。
选举专家们也庆祝了特朗普和今年投票中高调落选的候选人承认自己的失败。
“当然，我会接受（结果），”特朗普在选举之夜告诉福克斯新闻的布雷特·拜尔，因为民主党将重新夺回众议院和参议院已变得很明显。 “我为什么不呢？”
但仅仅几天后，他就开始对同样的结果进行阴谋论。
“有人真的相信这次‘选举’是诚实的吗？”特朗普在网上发帖称。
加州大学圣地亚哥分校的最新民意调查显示，在共和党人中，可能仍然有一些人接受这种说法。当被问及政客们对选民欺诈的讨论是否太多、太少或恰到好处时，只有 15% 的共和党人回答“太多”。
库塞尔说：“共和党基础选民要求继续关注这个问题，而且正如我们所看到的，即使在选举之后，政客们也在继续提供这一点。” “只要这两种动力存在，这些担忧仍然会有市场。”

title_en: Oath Keepers founder and Jan. 6 leader Stewart Rhodes is 'absolutely done' with Trump
title_zh: 誓言守护者组织创始人、1 月 6 日党魁斯图尔特·罗兹 (Stewart Rhodes) 与特朗普“彻底绝交”
summary: The founder of the right-wing militia known as the Oath Keepers says he's done with Donald Trump
summary_zh: 被称为“誓言守护者”的右翼民兵创始人表示，他与唐纳德·特朗普已经结束了
body_en: The founder of the right-wing militia known as the Oath Keepers says he's done with Donald Trump

IRVING, Texas -- IRVING, Texas (AP) — Stewart Rhodes didn’t just go to prison for Donald Trump . While serving time for his role in the Jan. 6 attack on the U.S. Capitol, the founder of the right-wing militia known as the Oath Keepers got a tattoo of Trump’s defiant face after he survived an assassin’s bullet in Butler, Pennsylvania .
It was further proof of Rhodes' devotion to the Republican president. But that's all over now.

“I am absolutely done with Trump,” said Rhodes, sitting at a rickety yellow table outside a gastropub in Irving, Texas. He considers Trump not just a traitor, but "one of the very worst in our nation's history.”

The repudiation from a former acolyte — one convicted of seditious conspiracy for orchestrating an ill-fated attempt to keep Trump in power six years ago — is another example of how allegiance to the president has faded even among extreme supporters. Back then, Rhodes claimed Trump lost the 2020 White House race to Democrat Joe Biden because of election fraud. This year in Texas, where Democrats had historic victories , he said there's another reason.

“The lion’s share is because Trump pissed off his own base," Rhodes said, his face shaded by a black cowboy hat. An eye patch covers his left socket, the result of an old gun accident, and a glacial blue iris peers out from the other.

Nearby, people mingled with drinks for his Christian Warriors After-Party, organized during a three-day conference called “Christ is King: America After Trump.” Some people approached to shake hands or sign up for the Oath Keepers or trainings for things like community defense and hurricane relief.

The beginning of Rhodes' break with Trump came when the president gave pardons to hundreds of people who were locked up for their actions on Jan. 6, 2021, but only commuted Rhodes' sentence . “That was the first inkling,” Rhodes said.

Rhodes also said Trump's war with Iran violated Trump's promises to end foreign conflicts. And, Rhodes said, it felt like an affront when Trump dismissed people who urged his administration to release files about the Jeffrey Epstein case , calling them “PAST supporters.” Then Rhodes felt Trump went back on his longtime slogan.

“We elected him to end the corruption in Washington, D.C. ‘Drain the swamp.’ Unfortunately his administration has been one of the most corrupt administrations in U.S. history," Rhodes said. “The pardons are pay-for-play and everything is pay-for-play.”

The White House did not respond to a request for comment. Rhodes is not alone in his about-face on Trump, but there's an ideological through line, said Sam Jackson, an associate professor at the University at Albany with a focus on anti-government extremism.

“They went from seeing Donald Trump as their ally in this fight against the conspiracy, to actually being co-opted by the conspiracy,” Jackson said, and it “points to deeper consistency in that understanding of the world as driven by hidden, evil actors.”

Rhodes, who graduated from Yale Law School and worked for former U.S. Rep. Ron Paul of Texas, founded the Oath Keepers in 2009 with the goal of encouraging members of the military and law enforcement to resist what they view as unconstitutional orders, such as disarming citizens or carrying out warrantless searches.
Army postpones plan to detonate nearly 10,000 pounds of lead azide until Monday
JPMorganChase, Mastercard, Visa report cyberattack on third-party service providers
Whipped cream sold at Costco in 12 states voluntarily recalled

Rhodes later allied himself with Trump's political movement, and the Oath Keepers supported his attempt to remain in office after losing the 2020 election. Fueled with conspiracies about voter fraud, prosecutors said group members gathered weapons, organized trainings and assembled in Washington , where some helped storm the Capitol on Jan. 6.
Rhodes, who did not enter the building that day, said he was a “political prisoner" who faced “illegality” in his trial. He was sentenced to 18 years, one of the longest sentences of any Jan. 6 case.

“You are smart, you are charismatic and compelling and frankly that’s what makes you dangerous,” U.S. District Judge Amit Mehta said during the hearing. “The moment you are released, whenever that may be, you will be ready to take up arms against your government.”
body_zh: 被称为“誓言守护者”的右翼民兵创始人表示，他与唐纳德·特朗普已经结束了
德克萨斯州欧文——德克萨斯州欧文（美联社）——斯图尔特·罗兹不仅仅因为唐纳德·特朗普入狱。右翼民兵组织“誓言守护者”的创始人因参与 1 月 6 日美国国会大厦袭击事件而服刑期间，在宾夕法尼亚州巴特勒市遭遇刺客子弹袭击后幸存下来，并纹上了特朗普挑衅面孔的纹身。
这进一步证明了罗德对共和党总统的忠诚。但现在一切都结束了。
“我绝对受够了特朗普，”罗德斯坐在德克萨斯州欧文一家美食酒吧外一张摇摇晃晃的黄色桌子旁说道。他认为特朗普不仅是一个叛徒，而且是“我们国家历史上最糟糕的叛徒之一”。
一名前助手的否认——六年前因策划一场不幸的企图让特朗普继续掌权而被判犯有煽动阴谋罪——的否认是另一个例子，说明即使在极端支持者中，对总统的忠诚度也已消失。当时，罗兹声称特朗普因选举舞弊而在 2020 年白宫竞选中输给了民主党人乔·拜登。今年在德克萨斯州，民主党取得了历史性胜利，他说还有另一个原因。
“最大的一部分是因为特朗普惹恼了他自己的支持者，”罗兹说，他的脸被黑色牛仔帽遮住了。他的左眼窝上戴着一个眼罩，那是一次旧枪事故造成的，而另一只眼罩则露出冰蓝色的虹膜。
在附近，人们在他的基督教勇士余兴派对上喝酒，该派对是在为期三天的名为“基督为王：特朗普之后的美国”会议期间组织的。有些人上前握手或报名参加誓言守护者或社区防御和飓风救援等培训。
罗兹与特朗普决裂的开始是在2021年1月6日，总统赦免了数百名因行为而被关押的人，但只是减刑了罗兹。 “这是第一个暗示，”罗兹说。
罗德还表示，特朗普与伊朗的战争违反了特朗普结束外国冲突的承诺。而且，罗兹说，当特朗普驳回那些敦促他的政府公布杰弗里·爱泼斯坦案文件的人时，称他们为“过去的支持者”，这感觉像是一种侮辱。然后罗兹觉得特朗普背弃了他长期以来的口号。
“我们选举他来结束华盛顿特区的腐败。‘排干沼泽’。不幸的是，他的政府是美国历史上最腐败的政府之一，”罗兹说。 “赦免是按场付费的，一切都是按场付费的。”
白宫没有回应置评请求。奥尔巴尼大学专注于反政府极端主义的副教授萨姆·杰克逊表示，罗德并不是唯一一个对特朗普态度大转变的人，但在意识形态上有一条明确的路线。
杰克逊说：“他们从将唐纳德·特朗普视为打击阴谋的盟友，到实际上被阴谋拉拢，这表明对世界的理解更加一致，认为世界是由隐藏的邪恶行为者驱动的。”
罗兹毕业于耶鲁大学法学院，曾为德克萨斯州前美国众议员罗恩·保罗工作，他于 2009 年创立了誓言守护者组织，旨在鼓励军队和执法人员抵制他们认为违宪的命令，例如解除公民武装或进行无证搜查。

罗兹后来与特朗普的政治运动结盟，誓言守护者组织也支持他在 2020 年大选失败后继续留任的努力。检察官称，在选民欺诈阴谋的推动下，该组织成员聚集了武器、组织培训并在华盛顿集结，其中一些人于 1 月 6 日帮助袭击了国会大厦。
罗德当天没有进入大楼，他说自己是一名“政治犯”，在审判中面临“非法”。他被判处 18 年徒刑，是 1 月 6 日案件中刑期最长的刑期之一。
美国地区法官阿米特·梅塔在听证会上表示：“你很聪明，很有魅力，引人注目，坦率地说，这就是你的危险之处。” “一旦你被释放，无论什么时候，你都会准备好拿起武器反对你的政府。”

title_en: ICE officers arrest 2 passengers boarding flight in Seattle
title_zh: ICE 官员在西雅图逮捕了 2 名正在登机的乘客
summary: Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday
summary_zh: 周六，当人们登机时，蒙面移民官员在西雅图一座拥挤的机场登机桥上逮捕了两名乘客
body_en: Masked immigration officers arrested two passengers on a crowded airport jet bridge in Seattle as people were boarding Saturday, federal officials said, causing what Alaska Airlines called a "distressing" scene for passengers and employees and delaying the Los Angeles-bound flight.
Videos of the incident showed officers dragging away at least one person at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport as a woman screamed that her daughter was being taken and she has a work permit.
Online flight data showed that Alaska Airlines Flight 1306, which had been scheduled to depart at 8:10 a.m., was delayed.
Alaska Airlines said U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officers gave no advance notice of the enforcement action, which occurred during a busy travel weekend ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday.

"We are concerned by this morning's law enforcement action during the boarding of Alaska Flight 1306," the airline said. "We recognize how distressing this incident has been for affected employees and guests."
It added that the airline is committed to "treating every guest with dignity and respect."

In a statement provided to CBS News Saturday evening, a spokesperson for the Department of Homeland Security, the parent agency of ICE, said that ICE officers "conducted a targeted enforcement operation" on a Mexican national identified as Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza who had "overstayed his visa."

During the arrest, a second passenger "hurled hot coffee" at the officers, the DHS spokesperson said in the statement. That second passenger, identified by DHS as Sofia Hernandez Mejia, is a Mexican national who had also been determined to have overstayed her visa, the spokesperson said.
Mejia was also subsequently arrested and will face federal charges of assaulting a federal officer, DHS said.
A DHS source told CBS News the two people arrested are a father and daughter.

Democratic Rep. Adam Smith of Washington said in an earlier statement that "masked ICE agents detained at least one passenger waiting to board an Alaska Airlines flight at Sea-Tac Airport. The masked agents forcibly dragged the individual off the jet bridge, taking them into custody."
The arresting officers wore unmarked jackets and khaki pants. Videos showed them struggling with someone on the ground as passengers surrounded by rolling suitcases looked on.

ICE has stepped up arrests at airports since the summer, especially targeting people who overstayed visas in the past. ICE sources told CBS News in July that the uptick in arrests stems from increased collaboration between ICE and the Transportation Security Administration.

On Thursday, a Princeton University student and Chinese national was detained by ICE at Ronald Reagan National Airport in Washington, D.C., after attending a neuroscience conference, the school and her colleagues said.

Alaska Airlines said it was working with the Port of Seattle, which manages the airport, to see if protocols were followed, and also that it has raised concerns "directly with the appropriate authorities."

The Port of Seattle said in a statement that the arrest was distressing not only for the affected family but for other passengers, and that local authorities would "engage federal officials to understand more about what occurred."
Washington Gov. Bob Ferguson, a Democrat, called the incident "just the latest example of ICE's deeply un-American tactics."

"ICE is completely and totally out of control," Ferguson said in a statement. "Like many Americans, I'm outraged by masked agents, who do not identify themselves, dragging people off jetways as they board a flight, creating chaos in our communities."

Democratic Rep. Pramila Jayapal of Washington said in a social media post that she was "disturbed by the reports of this detention at Sea-Tac," adding that her office was "working to gather more information on the situation."

DHS numbers obtained by CBS News last week found that ICE arrested 491,000 people in FY 2026, a record, including nearly 475,000 administrative arrests, also a record. Administrative arrests are those in which alleged undocumented immigrants are arrested for civil violations rather than criminal charges.
body_zh: 联邦官员称，周六，当人们登机时，蒙面移民官员在西雅图一座拥挤的机场登机桥上逮捕了两名乘客，造成阿拉斯加航空公司所说的乘客和员工“令人痛苦”的场景，并导致飞往洛杉矶的航班延误。
该事件的视频显示，警察在西雅图-塔科马国际机场拖走了至少一人，一名妇女尖叫着说她的女儿被带走了，而她有工作许可证。
在线航班数据显示，原定于上午8点10分起飞的阿拉斯加航空1306航班延误。
阿拉斯加航空公司表示，美国移民和海关执法局官员没有提前通知此次执法行动，此次执法行动发生在感恩节假期前繁忙的旅行周末。
该航空公司表示：“我们对今天早上阿拉斯加 1306 航班登机期间的执法行动感到担忧。” “我们认识到这一事件对受影响的员工和客人来说是多么痛苦。”
它还补充说，该航空公司致力于“以尊严和尊重对待每一位乘客”。
周六晚上向哥伦比亚广播公司新闻提供的一份声明中，ICE 的上级机构国土安全部发言人表示，ICE 官员对一名“签证逾期”的墨西哥公民里卡多·拉隆多·门多萨（Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza）“进行了有针对性的执法行动”。
国土安全部发言人在声明中表示，在逮捕过程中，另一名乘客向警察“投掷热咖啡”。该发言人表示，国土安全部确认的第二名乘客名叫索菲亚·埃尔南德斯·梅希亚，是一名墨西哥国民，她也被确定为签证逾期居留。
国土安全部表示，梅吉亚随后也被捕，并将面临袭击联邦官员的联邦指控。
国土安全部消息人士告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，被捕的两人是一对父女。
华盛顿的民主党众议员亚当·史密斯 (Adam Smith) 在早些时候的一份声明中表示，“蒙面 ICE 特工拘留了至少一名在西雅图-塔科马机场等待登机的阿拉斯加航空公司航班的乘客。蒙面特工强行将该人拖下登机桥，并将其拘留。”
逮捕的警察穿着没有标记的夹克和卡其布裤子。视频显示，他们与地面上的某人扭打在一起，周围都是滚滚行李箱的乘客在一旁观看。
自今年夏天以来，ICE 加大了在机场的逮捕力度，特别是针对过去签证逾期居留的人。 ICE 消息人士 7 月份告诉哥伦比亚广播公司新闻，逮捕人数的增加源于 ICE 和运输安全管理局之间加强合作。
普林斯顿大学及其同事表示，周四，一名中国公民在参加完神经科学会议后在华盛顿特区的罗纳德·里根国家机场被 ICE 拘留。
阿拉斯加航空公司表示，它正在与管理该机场的西雅图港合作，看看是否遵守了协议，并且已经“直接向有关当局”提出了担忧。
西雅图港在一份声明中表示，这次逮捕不仅让受影响的家庭感到痛苦，也让其他乘客感到痛苦，地方当局将“与联邦官员接触，以更多地了解所发生的事情”。
华盛顿州州长、民主党人鲍勃·弗格森称这一事件“只是 ICE 极不美国策略的最新例证”。
弗格森在一份声明中表示：“ICE 完全失控了。” “和许多美国人一样，我对蒙面特工感到愤怒，他们不肯透露自己的身份，在人们登机时将他们拖下飞机，在我们的社区制造混乱。”
华盛顿的民主党众议员普拉米拉·贾亚帕尔在社交媒体上发帖称，她“对西雅图-塔科马机场被拘留的报道感到不安”，并补充说她的办公室正在“努力收集有关情况的更多信息”。
哥伦比亚广播公司新闻上周获得的国土安全部数据显示，ICE 在 2026 财年逮捕了 491,000 人，创历史新高，其中包括近 475,000 人行政逮捕，也创历史新高。行政逮捕是指涉嫌无证移民因民事违法行为而不是刑事指控而被逮捕。

COVER STORY: Taking on credit card debt to buy food

This Thanksgiving, Americans are paying 32% more for food compared to what we paid in 2020. But according to a recent survey, about 35% of us are using credit cards to buy groceries – and many are having trouble paying off that food debt. Correspondent Lee Cowan looks at how rising costs, and the ease of Buy Now Pay Later apps, contribute to ever-tighter food budgets.
Kassandra Martinchek, senior researcher associate, Urban Institute

In California, more than 1,300 small kitchens are licensed to make and sell food. These MEHKOs (short for "micro enterprise home kitchen operations") are run out of homes, allowing cooks to pursue their passions, make supplementary income, or test out potential dining concepts without the investment required for food trucks or traditional brick-and-mortar restaurants. Correspondent Luke Burbank talked with some of the home chefs who turn family recipes into culinary passion projects.

Chain restaurants put a lot of America's supper clubs out of business in the 1950s and '60s, but the family-run dinner establishments continue to thrive in Wisconsin, built on Midwestern hospitality and friendliness. Correspondent Mo Rocca reports.

title_en: Democrats who swept into the Senate promised change. A leadership vote is testing them early
title_zh: 进入参议院的民主党人承诺进行变革。领导层投票正在尽早考验他们
summary: The Democratic Party’s incoming senators face an early test of their campaign promises to shake up Washington as they decide who will lead their new majority
summary_zh: 民主党即将上任的参议员在决定谁将领导他们的新民主党时，面临着他们的竞选承诺的早期考验，这些承诺将撼动华盛顿。
body_en: The Democratic Party’s incoming senators face an early test of their campaign promises to shake up Washington as they decide who will lead their new majority

WASHINGTON -- The Democratic Party’s incoming senators haven’t even been sworn into office yet, but the decision over who will lead their new majority is already testing the promise of change they made as candidates.

The 13 new Democrats are part of the largest incoming Senate class in decades, with several winning in Republican strongholds by promising to shake up Washington and be independent voices. Now they are caught up in a classic insider fight, forced to decide whether to stick with longtime Senate leader Chuck Schumer of New York or back challenger Chris Van Hollen of Maryland.

Newly elected progressives, including Abdul El-Sayed of Michigan and Peggy Flanagan of Minnesota, have backed Van Hollen, who is taking on Schumer with promises of a more aggressive legislative approach. Sen.-elect Sherrod Brown of Ohio, who is returning to Washington after losing his seat in 2024, supports Schumer.

But the incoming senators from traditionally Republican states such as Texas, Mississippi, Iowa and South Carolina, whose victories helped deliver Democrats the majority, have so far largely avoided taking sides. Annie Andrews of South Carolina has said she is talking with both candidates. Scott Colom of Mississippi says he wants to get to know them better before deciding and describes himself as being in “listening mode.”
Kansas Sen.-elect Adam Hamilton said Thursday he would not back Schumer, but declined to endorse anyone.
“I'm looking for someone who is going to bring people together,” Hamilton told MSNow. “Right now, in places like Kansas, there's a lot of people who don't feel that in Chuck Schumer.”

Schumer’s long-standing relationships and mastery of Senate machinery are a big advantage heading into the Dec. 1 vote, which will be held by secret ballot. But the reluctance of many incoming senators to commit has put an unusual spotlight on first-term lawmakers who could help shape the party’s direction in the new Congress.

“We should be very embracing of the new people who have been through fire to get here,” said Hawaii Sen. Mazie Hirono. “We have to make sure that all these voices are heard, and they’ve got a lot of talent to bring to the table.”
Many of the incoming senators campaigned as political outsiders , promising to bring fresh perspectives to a Washington establishment they argued had failed ordinary Americans.

Andrews, a 46-year-old pediatrician, became the first Democrat in nearly three decades to win a Senate race in South Carolina. She called for “generational change” and said that she would not support Schumer.
But she has also rejected policies that Van Hollen supports, such as “Medicare for All.” On a press call Tuesday, Andrews said she has made “no decision” on the majority leader's race.
“The way I assess the situation as it is right now is that the generational change is represented by this incredibly dynamic incoming freshman class of senators,” Andrews said.

Texas Sen.-elect James Talarico called for “new blood” in the Democratic Party, arguing that fresh perspectives were needed to change a political system that had failed. But Talarico has stopped short of rejecting Schumer, saying in a CBS interview two days after the Nov. 3 election that he would meet with the leadership candidates and ask “tough questions.”

Iowa Sen.-elect Josh Turek has taken a similar approach, saying his decision will depend on which candidate best reflects the priorities he campaigned on. During a news conference Monday, he said that he had met with Schumer and Van Hollen and was waiting for “further updates” on questions he had.

“Whoever provides those answers to me that most closely align with my common sense, prairie populist agenda that I’ve been running on for the last year and a half, that’s who I’ll support,” Turek said.
Alaska Sen.-elect Mary Peltola, whose race was officially called on Wednesday , told The Associated Press soon after that she had not yet thought about the leadership race.
